characters.description: An eighteen-year-old student at the Capitol's elite Academy, the last hope of the once-powerful Snow family, which was ruined by the war against the districts and now hides its poverty behind a proud name. Ambitious, calculating, and desperate to win a university scholarship that could restore the family fortunes, he is charming and self-possessed on the surface while privately obsessed with status and survival. When the Academy makes its top students mentors to the tributes of the tenth Hunger Games, his future comes to depend on how his assigned tribute performs.
characters.name: Coriolanus Snow

characters.description: Coriolanus's older cousin, who has helped raise him and keep the impoverished Snow household afloat. Warm, self-sacrificing, and quietly clever, she works as an apprentice to a fashion designer and does whatever she can to protect her cousin's prospects, including altering his father's old shirts so he can appear respectable. She is his closest confidante and moral anchor.
characters.name: Tigris Snow

characters.description: The listless, contemptuous Dean of the Academy, often visibly under the influence of a narcotic. From the start he treats Coriolanus with pointed dislike that the young man cannot explain, needling and slighting him at every turn. An authority over the mentorship program, he holds real power over Coriolanus's future while seeming to wish him ill.
characters.name: Dean Casca Highbottom

characters.description: Coriolanus's Academy classmate and uneasy friend, the son of a District 2 munitions magnate whose new wealth bought the family Capitol citizenship. Sensitive and principled, Sejanus is sickened by the Hunger Games and openly sympathetic to the districts he came from, which makes him an outsider among his snobbish peers. His conscience repeatedly puts him at odds with the Capitol and in danger.
characters.name: Sejanus Plinth

characters.description: A studious, competitive classmate of Coriolanus at the Academy and one of his fellow mentors. Ambitious and eager to impress the Gamemakers, she works closely with him on a written assignment about the future of the Games early in the story.
characters.name: Clemensia Dovecote

characters.description: The girl tribute reaped from District 12 for the tenth Hunger Games and Coriolanus's mentoring assignment. A performer with the Covey, a family of traveling musicians, she dresses in a bright ruffled rainbow dress and turns her own reaping into a defiant spectacle, singing to the crowd and startling the mayor's daughter with a snake. Charismatic, resourceful, and unafraid to command an audience, she treats attention as a survival tool. Coriolanus first sees her as a hopeless assignment and quickly realizes she may be the most memorable tribute of them all.
characters.name: Lucy Gray Baird

characters.description: The Capitol's Head Gamemaker and chief scientist, a white-haired woman with unsettling, mismatched eyes who designs the muttations and the cruelties of the Hunger Games. Brilliant, theatrical, and utterly without pity, she runs experiments on humans and creatures alike and takes an interest in Coriolanus, testing his ideas and his nerve. She views the Games as a demonstration of her bleak philosophy about human nature.
characters.name: Dr. Volumnia Gaul

characters.description: A loud, boastful Academy classmate of Coriolanus and a fellow mentor, from a well-connected Capitol family. She enjoys showing off and taunting the tributes, treating the whole spectacle as a chance for personal attention.
characters.name: Arachne Crane

characters.description: The boy tribute reaped from District 12 alongside Lucy Gray, a quiet, protective young man who shields her during the brutal journey to the Capitol. Loyal to his district partner, he stays close to her among the caged tributes.
characters.name: Jessup

characters.description: Lucy Gray's former sweetheart back in District 12, once a member of the Covey band. His betrayal of her before the reaping still stings, and his entanglements in the district cause fresh trouble when Coriolanus arrives there.
characters.name: Billy Taupe

characters.description: The youngest member of the Covey, Lucy Gray's musical family in District 12. A quick, bright child with a remarkable memory for songs, she performs with the band and is devoted to Lucy Gray.
characters.name: Maude Ivory

recaps.ending: Coriolanus gets Lucy Gray through the tenth Hunger Games alive, partly by secretly handling Dr. Gaul's venomous snakes so they will not strike her, but his rule-breaking is discovered and he is stripped of the scholarship he needed. To avoid disgrace and punishment he enlists as a Peacekeeper and is posted to District 12, where he reunites with Lucy Gray and the Covey. His conscience-stricken friend Sejanus Plinth conspires with local rebels; Coriolanus reports him to Dr. Gaul, and Sejanus is hanged. Terrified that his own crimes, including killings he committed, will surface, Coriolanus plans to run away north with Lucy Gray, but at a lakeside cabin they uncover the hidden guns and he realizes the evidence ties him to murder. He turns on her in the woods; she disappears among the mockingjays and he fires blindly, never finding her body. Returning to the Capitol, he is welcomed by Dr. Gaul as a promising protege, discovers that Dean Highbottom devised the Hunger Games from his dead father's idea, and coldly secures his own rise. The boy who began desperate and charming ends the book hardened into the ruthless future President Snow.
recaps.in_short: Decades before Katniss, eighteen-year-old Coriolanus Snow is a proud but secretly impoverished Capitol student staking his future on the tenth Hunger Games, where Academy students now mentor the tributes. Assigned the District 12 girl, Lucy Gray Baird, a charismatic singer with the traveling Covey, he schemes to keep her alive and popular, inventing sponsorship and betting to draw the Capitol's attention, and falls for her along the way. He bends and breaks the rules to help her win, even tampering with the Gamemakers' venomous snakes, and she survives the arena. But his cheating is exposed; stripped of his prize, he enlists as a Peacekeeper and is sent to District 12, where he reunites with Lucy Gray. When his friend Sejanus becomes entangled with rebels, Coriolanus informs on him and Sejanus is executed. Fleeing north with Lucy Gray, Coriolanus finds evidence of his own crimes and turns on her; she vanishes into the woods, and he returns to the Capitol to be rewarded by Dr. Gaul, stepping onto the path that will make him President Snow.

recaps.text: Ten years after the war between the Capitol and the districts, the Hunger Games are still a shabby, unpopular spectacle. To boost interest, the Academy assigns its top students as mentors to the twenty-four tributes of the tenth Games. Coriolanus Snow, heir to a fallen Capitol family that hides its poverty behind its famous name, is dismayed to draw the girl from District 12, Lucy Gray Baird. At her reaping she stunned the crowd by singing and by dropping a snake down the mayor's daughter's dress, and she performs with the traveling musicians called the Covey. The tributes are shipped to the Capitol and locked in the monkey house of the old zoo, treated as animals. Sensing that Lucy Gray's showmanship could make her memorable, Coriolanus visits her openly at the zoo, begins to win the Capitol's sympathy for her, and pushes the idea that citizens should be able to sponsor and gamble on individual tributes. His idealistic friend Sejanus Plinth, meanwhile, is increasingly sickened by the whole enterprise.

As the Games approach, the mentors' new sponsorship and betting schemes start to change how the Capitol watches. A rebel bombing tears through the arena during a pre-Games visit, killing and injuring several people and briefly trapping Coriolanus and some tributes; the Gamemakers press ahead regardless. The boastful mentor Arachne Crane is killed by her own starving tribute during a broadcast, a shock that underlines how dangerous the spectacle is. Coriolanus grows genuinely attached to Lucy Gray and keeps finding ways, some against the rules, to feed her, protect her reputation, and funnel sponsor gifts to her. When the tenth Hunger Games finally begin in the damaged arena, tributes die quickly and violently, but Lucy Gray survives the early carnage by hiding, staying mobile, and relying on the quiet help Coriolanus smuggles to her. Dr. Gaul, the Head Gamemaker, watches Coriolanus closely, testing his instincts and drawing him deeper into her grim view of human nature.

Lucy Gray wins the tenth Hunger Games. In the final stretch Coriolanus secretly enters Dr. Gaul's laboratory and handles her tank of brightly colored venomous snakes so that they will recognize Lucy Gray's scent and leave her unharmed when they are released into the arena, and she outlasts the last of her rivals to claim victory. Their bond feels, to him, like love. But the ways he cheated to help her are uncovered, and instead of the scholarship and glory he expected, Coriolanus is disgraced and faces exposure. To escape punishment and start over, he enlists in the Peacekeepers, the Capitol's military police, and is shipped out to a posting in far-off District 12, the very district Lucy Gray comes from. Sejanus, wracked by guilt, uses his family's money to enlist alongside him. Arriving in District 12, Coriolanus is reunited with Lucy Gray and her Covey family and tries to imagine a future with her, even as the Capitol's reach and his own secrets follow him.

In District 12, Coriolanus and Lucy Gray rekindle their romance while he serves as a Peacekeeper, but the district seethes with unrest. Sejanus, still tormented by conscience, conspires with local rebels to help people escape north. Coriolanus, fearing the plot will doom them both, informs on Sejanus to Dr. Gaul through a jabberjay recording, and Sejanus is arrested and hanged, a betrayal Coriolanus hides from everyone. When his own crimes, including killings he committed, threaten to come to light, Coriolanus agrees to flee into the wilderness with Lucy Gray. At a cabin by a lake they discover a cache of hidden guns, and he realizes one of them can tie him to murder. His paranoia curdles into a decision to silence her. Alone in the woods, Lucy Gray sees what he is and slips away among the singing mockingjays; he fires wildly into the trees but never finds her. Coriolanus returns to the Capitol, where Dr. Gaul rewards him with a place at the university and a future in power. He learns that Dean Highbottom created the Hunger Games from an idea Coriolanus's own father twisted, settles that score, and steps fully into the ruthless man who will one day rule Panem as President Snow.

characters.description: Months after he shot the governor of Elendel in front of the city, Waxillium Ladrian is a divisive figure at home and no longer on speaking terms with his god. He is Twinborn, a Coinshot who Pushes on metal and a Skimmer who can change his own weight, and he is finally about to marry Steris Harms. He is also carrying the knowledge that the woman he loved in the Roughs was never who he thought she was, and that Harmony arranged it, which has left him with a great deal of anger and nowhere useful to put it.
characters.name: Waxillium Ladrian

characters.description: Wax's partner, a Twinborn Slider and Bloodmaker whose bendalloy bubble accelerates time around him and whose stored gold heals injuries that should be fatal. He fights with a duelling cane, refuses to carry a gun, collects hats, and can become almost anyone with an accent and the right coat. He is involved with the kandra MeLaan, which suits them both and alarms most people who hear about it.
characters.name: Wayne

characters.description: A constable with a growing reputation, and the member of the group most likely to have read something relevant. She has stopped waiting to be given permission to lead, and she is far more interested in the historical and scholarly side of this case than anyone expects a police officer to be.
characters.name: Marasi Colms

characters.description: Wax's betrothed, whose wedding preparations are as thorough as her contingency plans. She is socially awkward and entirely aware of it, and she packs for eventualities other people would consider absurd, which is repeatedly why the group survives them.
characters.name: Steris Harms

characters.description: A kandra, one of the Faceless Immortals who serve Harmony, and by now a fixture of Wax's circle. She can reshape her borrowed body at will, enjoys the physical world far more than her elders think proper, and treats a dangerous assignment as a holiday.
characters.name: MeLaan

characters.description: The god of this world, once a Terris scholar named Sazed. Wax is not speaking to him at the start of this book, having learned how far Harmony's arrangement of his life went. Harmony still runs the kandra, still knows more than he says, and is more constrained than the people who pray to him have ever been told.
characters.name: Harmony

characters.description: A kandra scholar, fussy and academic where MeLaan is neither, who acts as the kandra's liaison to Wax. He brings the case that starts the book and is considerably more interested in evidence, provenance and correct citation than in the danger attached to any of it.
characters.name: VenDell

characters.description: A kandra sent south to investigate rumors, who has come back missing one of his spikes. Kandra hold their minds in their spikes, so without it he is confused and barely coherent, but he returned carrying an image of a metal bracer that may be the thing generations of scholars have been looking for.
characters.name: ReLuur

characters.description: A gunsmith from the Roughs who outfits Wax and his people for a long trip south. Precise, private, and entirely done with pretending Wayne's attentions are charming.
characters.name: Ranette

characters.description: A noblewoman of New Seran whose estate is the social center of that city and whose interests are aligned with the Set. The party she hosts is the group's way into what the organization has been doing in the south.
characters.name: Kelesina Shores

characters.description: A young sky-sailor from the Malwish, a nation on the southern continent that the Basin had assumed was uninhabited ice. His people wear masks in public and build machines the Basin cannot: flying ships, and medallions, unkeyed metalminds that let anyone at all draw on Feruchemical attributes without being born to the art. He speaks the Basin's language with enormous enthusiasm and very poor accuracy. His expedition was destroyed and he was left behind alone.
characters.name: Allik Neromnian

characters.description: Wax's uncle, alive despite a reported death, and a senior figure in the Set, where he is known as Suit. He is calm, precise and genuinely convinced that the organization's work is necessary, and he treats his nephew as a problem of management rather than as family.
characters.name: Edwarn Ladrian

characters.description: Wax's older sister, believed killed years ago alongside their uncle, and in fact alive and in the Set's hands. Sharp-tongued and unsentimental, she is close to a stranger to Wax now, and getting her out is the thing he wants most from this expedition.
characters.name: Telsin Ladrian

characters.description: The figure the Malwish credit with founding their nation and giving them their technology, buried in the temple at the heart of this book. The evidence in the tomb identifies him as Kelsier, the Survivor of the Final Empire's fall, who did not stay dead when he was killed three centuries ago and who crossed to the southern continent after the world was remade.
characters.name: the Sovereign

recaps.ending: Wax puts on the Bands of Mourning and, with Feruchemical reserves on a scale nothing living has held since the Lord Ruler, breaks the Set's operation at the temple, brings down their transport and gets his people out. The victory is partial. Edwarn Ladrian escapes, and Telsin leaves with him: Wax's sister is not the prisoner he came to rescue, and has not been for a long time. Allik Neromnian survives and becomes the Basin's first real contact with the Malwish, whose medallion technology, capable of granting Feruchemical attributes to people not born to the art, is a change to the world that nobody has begun to absorb. The burial chamber Marasi found is the tomb of the figure the Malwish call the Sovereign, and the evidence in it identifies him as Kelsier, the Survivor of Era 1, who outlived his own death and founded a nation on the southern continent. Back in Elendel, Wax and Steris marry. Wax puts his earring back in and speaks to Harmony again, and Harmony finally tells him what he has been withholding: the Set serves another god, called Trell, one of several powers that exist beyond this world, and Harmony is bound in ways he has never admitted. Wax keeps the Bands. The Basin ends the book knowing it is neither alone on its own planet nor alone in the universe, and the Set is still moving.
recaps.in_short: Months after the death of Elendel's governor, the kandra bring Waxillium Ladrian a case: one of their own has come back from the far south damaged and short a spike, carrying an image of a bracer that may be the Bands of Mourning, the metalminds said to have made the Lord Ruler unstoppable. Wax, Wayne, Marasi, Steris and the kandra MeLaan travel to New Seran, where the Set is already established, and their attempt to work the city ends in a fight and a flight. Following the Set out of the mountains they find a hidden airship and Allik Neromnian, a survivor of the Malwish, an advanced nation on the southern continent nobody in the Basin knew existed, whose medallions let ordinary people use Feruchemy. They fly to a buried temple, where the Set captures them and Wax faces his uncle Edwarn. Marasi finds a tomb at its heart belonging to the Malwish founder, whose identity ties the southern continent back to Kelsier, the Survivor. Wax claims the Bands and wrecks the Set's operation, but Edwarn escapes with Telsin, who proves to be with the Set willingly. Wax marries Steris, takes Harmony back, and learns that the Set serves a rival god called Trell.

recaps.text: Background: three centuries ago this world was ash-choked and ruled by an immortal tyrant. A thief called Kelsier began the rebellion that unseated him and died doing it; a young woman named Vin finished it, and later destroyed the god of decay at the cost of her own life. A Terris scholar named Sazed took up the divine powers left behind, became Harmony, and remade the planet into somewhere people could live. Kelsier is worshipped as the Survivor, Vin as the Ascendant Warrior, and their descendants have built the Elendel Basin into a place of railways, electric light and revolvers, where Allomancy and Feruchemy survive thinned into single-power Mistings and Twinborn. Previously: Waxillium Ladrian gave up twenty years as a lawman in the frontier Roughs and came home to run House Ladrian. With his partner Wayne and the constable Marasi Colms he broke a gang whose abductions served a secret organization called the Set, and found that his uncle Edwarn had faked his death and joined it. A year later a rogue kandra called Bleeder set out to break Elendel and maneuvered Wax into shooting Governor Innate in public, in the belief that he was killing her in disguise. She then revealed that she was Paalm, the kandra Harmony had assigned to watch over Wax, who had lived as his beloved Lessie and staged her death at his hands. Wax killed her, then rejected Harmony and set aside the earring the god spoke through. Elendel is still without a functioning government, the Set's purchase on it has been exposed, and Wax and Steris Harms are engaged and not yet married.

Elendel is still unsettled after the death of its governor, and Waxillium Ladrian, who fired the shot, is a divisive figure in a city that cannot decide whether he saved it. He is also, at last, about to marry Steris Harms, and he is not speaking to Harmony. Then the kandra bring him a case. One of their number, ReLuur, was sent to the far south to chase rumors and has come back damaged, missing one of the spikes that holds his mind together and barely able to explain himself. What he brought back is an image of a metal bracer that may be part of the Bands of Mourning, the legendary metalminds said to have been the source of the Lord Ruler's power. The kandra scholar VenDell wants Wax to go south to New Seran, confirm what ReLuur found, and recover the missing spike. Wax, Wayne, Marasi, MeLaan and Steris take the train.

New Seran is a mountain city in the far south of the Basin where Elendel's authority is resented and its money is not. The group works two problems at once: finding out who has been buying up every rumor about the Bands, and recovering ReLuur's stolen spike from the people who took it. Their route into the first is a party at the estate of a local noblewoman with Set connections, where Steris's exhaustive preparation and Marasi's nerve get them considerably further than Wax's reputation does. Wayne and MeLaan handle the spike by their own methods. The evening ends badly: the Set already knew they were coming, the house turns hostile, and they have to fight their way out with what they have learned. It is clear the Set has been established in New Seran for years, and that it is not chasing a legend out of curiosity.

Following the Set's trail out of the city, the group finds something nobody in the Basin knew existed: a concealed cache holding a flying machine, and with it a survivor of the people who built it. Allik Neromnian comes from the Malwish, a nation on the southern continent that the Basin had assumed was empty ice. The Malwish have technology the Basin cannot imagine, built on medallions, unkeyed metalminds that let anyone at all draw on Feruchemical attributes without being born to the art. Allik's expedition was destroyed by the Set. With his help the group takes the airship and flies for the site where the Bands are supposed to lie, ahead of the Set but not by much.

The party reaches a temple buried in the mountains and goes inside. It was built by whoever founded the Malwish, and it is full of machinery and writing that ties the southern continent's history to the Basin's and both back to the fall of the Final Empire. The Set arrives in force, led by Wax's uncle Edwarn Ladrian, whom the organization calls Suit. The group is broken up and part of it taken. Wax and Suit face each other for the first time since Wax learned his uncle was alive, and Suit makes it plain that the Set's plans are much larger than a stolen relic, and that the organization answers to a patron it calls Trell. Wax also finds his sister Telsin, believed killed years ago alongside their uncle, alive and held by the Set.

Held inside the temple complex, the group works in pieces. Marasi pushes deeper into the structure and finds a burial chamber at its heart, raised for a figure the southerners call the Sovereign, who founded their nation and left them their technology. Wayne and MeLaan cause the kind of trouble they are best at. Steris, a captive with a very large bag, keeps producing things nobody else thought to bring. Wax gets loose and goes after his sister and the Bands at the same time, while the Set moves to take the prize and leave before the mountain and its machinery can be turned against them.

Wax reaches the Bands of Mourning and puts them on. They hold Feruchemical storage on a scale nothing living has carried since the Lord Ruler, giving him strength, speed, weight, healing and more all at once and in quantity, and with them he wrecks the Set's operation, brings down their transport and gets his people out. It is not a clean win. Edwarn escapes, and Telsin goes with him: she is not the prisoner Wax believed he was rescuing and has been working with the Set. The burial chamber Marasi found is identified as the tomb of the Sovereign, and the evidence in it points at Kelsier, the Survivor of Era 1, who did not stay dead and who crossed to the southern continent and founded the Malwish nation there. Allik survives to become the Basin's first contact with his people, whose medallions can hand Feruchemy to anyone. Back in Elendel, Wax and Steris marry. Wax puts his earring back in and speaks to Harmony again, and Harmony tells him the rest: the Set serves Trell, another god, one of several powers beyond this world, and Harmony is bound in ways he had never admitted. Wax keeps the Bands.

characters.description: A Ranger's apprentice from Araluen, hiding in a mountain cabin in Skandia after months as a slave. He is physically wrecked and only recently through withdrawal from the drug the Skandians fed their labour gangs, and he has to rebuild both his strength and his confidence in the skills Halt taught him. He is quick, observant and better at improvising than he gives himself credit for.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: Will's companion in the mountains, who nursed him through withdrawal and has kept them both alive through a Skandian winter. She is really Cassandra, King Duncan's daughter and heir to Araluen, and cannot say so anywhere in Skandia, because the Oberjarl Ragnak has sworn a blood oath against her family. Resourceful, obstinate and unwilling to be treated as cargo by anybody.
characters.name: Evanlyn

characters.description: A Ranger of Araluen, banished from his own country for a year so that he could come after his apprentice, and now deep inside Skandia with no authority and no friends. He is the best tactical mind in the story, patient, sardonic, and prepared to make an alliance with anyone if it serves the people he is protecting.
characters.name: Halt

characters.description: A young Araluen warrior travelling with Halt, still formally a Battleschool apprentice and already one of the best swordsmen either country has seen. He killed Morgarath in single combat and a Gallic warlord after him, and he is loyal, direct and steady when things go wrong.
characters.name: Horace Altman

characters.description: An eastern people of horse warriors whose scouting parties are appearing in the Skandian mountains. They fight as disciplined mounted archers in large formations, ride small tough ponies, and move faster than any force in the west. They are scouting the country as a preliminary to taking it.
characters.name: The Temujai

characters.description: A Skandian jarl and wolfship captain, the man who captured Will and Evanlyn and later helped them escape Hallasholm. He is loud, blunt and greedy by trade, and steadier and more honourable than any of that suggests. He has influence among the jarls and will spend it if he thinks the cause is right.
characters.name: Erak

characters.description: Erak's second in command, cheerfully loyal and quick to follow his jarl into anything.
characters.name: Svengal

characters.description: The Oberjarl of Skandia, absolute among his own people and violently impatient with advice, particularly from foreigners. He has sworn the Vallasvow, a blood oath binding him to kill the royal family of Araluen, which makes him the single greatest danger to Evanlyn in the country.
characters.name: Ragnak

characters.description: The Oberjarl's hilfmann, who runs Hallasholm's stores, accounts and slave labour. Unwarlike and permanently anxious, he is the one Skandian in authority who thinks in terms of numbers and supply, which makes him unexpectedly useful once an invasion is coming.
characters.name: Borsa

characters.description: The general commanding the Temujai force moving on Skandia: experienced, methodical, and contemptuous of an enemy he expects to overrun. He plans in terms of ground, remounts and lines of advance rather than of individual glory.
characters.name: Haz'kam

recaps.ending: The Temujai invasion is broken. Halt's plan holds: the Skandian line gives ground where it is meant to, the Temujai cavalry is drawn into ground it cannot use, and the Araluen archers, commanded by Will after Halt is wounded, break the charge that was supposed to end the battle. The eastern army withdraws, and Skandia survives as an independent country because two escaped Araluen slaves and a banished Ranger chose to warn it. In the aftermath Evanlyn's identity comes out. Ragnak's Vallasvow would bind him to kill her, but he does not survive the battle, and the Skandian leadership that follows, with Erak's weight behind it, sets the oath aside rather than begin a war it has just finished paying for. What is agreed instead is a treaty: peace between Skandia and Araluen, the freeing of the Araluen slaves, including the men who fought as Halt's archers, and an alliance between two countries that have spent a generation raiding one another. Halt's banishment, engineered so that he could leave, is lifted by King Duncan, who has his daughter and his Ranger back. The Araluens sail home. Will has come through addiction, slavery and a battle, and returns to finish an apprenticeship that now looks very different.
recaps.in_short: Halt and Horace finally reach the mountain cabin where Evanlyn has nursed Will through warmweed withdrawal, but Temujai scouts, eastern horse warriors probing Skandia, seize Evanlyn first, and the three Araluens have to track the raiders and take her back. What they learn doing it is that a Temujai army is about to invade Skandia. Escaped slaves and enemies though they are, they carry the warning to Hallasholm, where Erak's backing and Halt's usefulness buy them a hearing from the Oberjarl Ragnak, while Evanlyn's royal identity stays hidden because of Ragnak's blood oath against her family. Skandians despise the bow, so Halt and Will train the Araluen slaves into an archery corps in exchange for their freedom, and Halt plans a battle around ground the Temujai cavalry cannot use. In the fighting Halt is wounded and Will commands the archers; the invasion is broken and Ragnak is killed. Evanlyn's identity emerges, the oath dies with him, and Skandia and Araluen make peace, free the slaves and send the Araluens home.

recaps.text: Previously: Will, an orphan ward of Castle Redmont, was apprenticed to the Ranger Halt and helped destroy the Kalkara sent by the rebel lord Morgarath. When Morgarath invaded Araluen, Will, his friend Horace and a girl called Evanlyn burned the bridge Morgarath's slaves had built to outflank the King's army. Horace escaped and Morgarath was killed in single combat by him, ending the war, but Will and Evanlyn were captured by the Skandian jarl Erak and carried north. Evanlyn turned out to be Cassandra, King Duncan's daughter and heir to Araluen, travelling under another name. Refused permission to go after his apprentice, Halt got himself banished for a year by publicly insulting the King, and travelled with Horace through lawless Gallica, where they were held by the warlord Deparnieux until Horace killed him in a formal challenge. In Skandia, Will and Evanlyn were made slaves at Hallasholm under the Oberjarl Ragnak, who has sworn a blood oath against Araluen's royal family. Will was sent to the labour yard and made dependent on warmweed, the drug used to keep the slaves docile. Erak helped the pair escape before winter, and Evanlyn took Will to a mountain cabin and forced him through withdrawal while Halt and Horace pressed north to find them.

Will is recovering in the mountain cabin, weak and shaky but himself again, when the isolation ends badly: a Temujai scouting party, eastern horsemen ranging through the Skandian mountains, takes Evanlyn. Halt and Horace, who have crossed Gallica and worked their way into Skandia searching, reach the cabin and find Will alone. The reunion is brief. With Will barely able to draw a bow and the raiders already moving, the three of them set out after the scouting party to get Evanlyn back, and Halt begins to gauge how far his apprentice has actually come back from what the yard did to him.

The three Araluens take Evanlyn back from the Temujai, using Halt's shooting and Horace's sword against a party that outnumbers them, and Will proves he can still do the work when it matters. What they learn from the encounter is more serious than the rescue: the scouts are not raiders but the leading edge of a Temujai army, and Skandia is being surveyed for invasion. The Skandians, who have no idea what is coming, fight as individual axemen and have never faced disciplined mounted archers. The four of them are escaped slaves and enemies of the country, but Halt concludes that they have to carry the warning to Hallasholm, and that the alternative is a massacre.

They reach Hallasholm and are taken by the Skandians, which is the easy part; getting the Oberjarl Ragnak to listen to a banished Araluen Ranger is not. Erak, who captured Will and Evanlyn in the first place and helped them escape, vouches for them, and Borsa the hilfmann grasps the logistics of what is coming. Ragnak, contemptuous but not stupid, accepts the warning and grudgingly accepts Halt's help with it. Evanlyn stays Evanlyn, since Ragnak's blood oath against the royal house of Araluen would oblige him to kill Cassandra on sight, and only a handful of people know how thin the disguise is.

Halt studies the problem and finds the Skandian army's flaw: superb close-quarters fighters with no missile arm at all, facing an enemy whose whole method is to shoot from horseback and never close until the enemy is broken. Skandians regard the bow as a coward's weapon, so Halt looks elsewhere for archers and finds them among the Araluen slaves, hundreds of countrymen with nothing to lose. He and Will train them into a disciplined corps in the time available, with freedom promised in exchange, while the Skandians prepare a defensive position in the pass above Hallasholm. The Temujai general Haz'kam, meanwhile, moves his army west, expecting the campaign to be short.

The first clashes go as Halt predicted: Temujai horse archers cut up Skandian formations that cannot reach them, and the invaders learn nothing to change their opinion of the defenders. That is deliberate. Halt's plan turns on the Temujai believing what they have seen, and on ground where cavalry cannot manoeuvre, with the Araluen archers concealed until the decisive moment. The Skandian jarls have to accept a battle plan built on a feigned retreat, which runs against everything their fighting tradition values, and Will takes practical command of the archer corps he has spent weeks training.

The main battle is fought in the pass. The Skandian line gives ground on cue, the Temujai commit to what looks like a rout, and the trap closes on ground that ruins their mobility. Halt is wounded during the fighting and Will is left to command the archers at the point where the plan either works or fails, giving the shooting orders that break the Temujai charge. The battle is savage and the Skandian losses are heavy, but the invasion is stopped rather than merely delayed, and the eastern army is forced to withdraw.

The Temujai retreat and Skandia survives, saved by a plan devised by a banished Araluen Ranger and executed in part by Araluen slaves. In the aftermath Evanlyn's real name comes out. The Vallasvow would bind Ragnak to kill her, but he is killed in the battle, and the leadership that follows, with Erak behind it, sets the oath aside. What is agreed instead is a treaty between Skandia and Araluen: peace, an alliance, and freedom for the Araluen slaves, including the men who fought as archers. King Duncan lifts Halt's banishment, which was only ever a device to let him leave, and the Araluens sail home with Cassandra restored to her father. Will, who arrived in Skandia as a drugged slave, leaves it having commanded an army's archers, and returns to Redmont to finish his apprenticeship.

characters.description: A fourteen-year-old demigod son of Poseidon, starting high school in the mortal world while war with the Titans draws closer. Loyal and stubborn, he joins a dangerous quest into an ancient maze to keep the enemy from using it to strike at his camp, and he carries the growing weight of a prophecy about a child of the eldest gods.
characters.name: Percy Jackson

characters.description: A red-haired mortal girl Percy meets at high school orientation. Unlike most humans, she can see through the Mist that hides monsters and magic from ordinary people, which lets her perceive danger, and demigods, clearly. Bold and artistic, she becomes an unexpected help to Percy when he needs a guide who can navigate by sight where magic misleads.
characters.name: Rachel Elizabeth Dare

characters.description: A demigod daughter of Athena and Percy's closest friend, a gifted planner and fighter with a lifelong fascination for architecture and for the legendary inventor Daedalus. She is given her first chance to lead a quest of her own, into the Labyrinth, and feels the strain of command and of old, unresolved feelings about Luke.
characters.name: Annabeth Chase

characters.description: A satyr and Percy's devoted friend, under pressure from the Council of Cloven Elders to find the lost wild god Pan or lose his searcher's license. He joins the quest into the maze, still driven by his hope of finding Pan and carrying the burden of a promise he must keep.
characters.name: Grover Underwood

characters.description: A young Cyclops and Percy's half-brother, son of Poseidon, who has been working in the undersea forges. Gentle, immensely strong, and skilled with metal and machines, he rejoins Percy for the quest and forms a special bond with an ancient hundred-handed creature they encounter in the maze.
characters.name: Tyson

characters.description: A son of Hades, grown solitary and grim since his sister Bianca's death, which he blames on Percy. Able to summon and command the dead, he is shadowed by a scheming ghost who urges him toward revenge and toward a bargain to bring his sister back. Powerful and unpredictable, he moves through the Underworld and the maze on his own errands.
characters.name: Nico di Angelo

characters.description: The god of fire, forges, and craftsmanship, who makes his workshops in volcanoes and builds mechanical wonders. Gruff and wary of being used, he agrees to help the questers only if Percy first investigates who has been intruding on one of his forges, sending Percy toward a dangerous confrontation beneath a mountain.
characters.name: Hephaestus

characters.description: An immortal nymph, daughter of a Titan, exiled to the hidden island of Ogygia and cursed to be found only rarely by a hero she cannot keep. Gentle and lonely, she nurses Percy back to health after he is gravely hurt and grows fond of him, offering a peaceful life on the island that he must decide whether to accept.
characters.name: Calypso

characters.description: The legendary inventor who built the Labyrinth in ancient times and has kept himself alive across the ages by transferring his mind into a series of automaton bodies. He has recently been living at the demigod camp disguised as a new sword instructor named Quintus. Brilliant and burdened by old guilt, he holds the secret to controlling the maze that both sides now seek.
characters.name: Daedalus

characters.description: The ancient god of the wild, lost for millennia and sought by generations of satyrs, including Grover. Found at last deep within the maze, he is fading as the wild places of the world dwindle. Weary and at peace, he entrusts his work to those who find him, asking them to carry his spirit forward as the old order passes.
characters.name: Pan

characters.description: A demigod son of Hermes who leads the Titan lord's army against the gods. He seeks the means to master the Labyrinth so his forces can invade the demigod camp from within. Ruthless and determined, he is preparing for the final rise of his master, and remains a painful figure to Annabeth, who once trusted him.
characters.name: Luke Castellan

characters.description: The ancient Titan lord, nearly fully re-formed from his scattered remains and hungry to overthrow the gods who cast him down. His growing power drives the enemy's assault on the demigods, and his return draws steadily closer as his followers prepare the way for him to take physical form.
characters.name: Kronos

recaps.ending: Luke's Titan army invades Camp Half-Blood through the Labyrinth, and in the battle the inventor Daedalus, having helped the defenders, chooses to end his long life; his death collapses the maze and permanently cuts off the enemy's shortcut into the camp, though the fighting costs demigod lives. The lost wild god Pan has died deep in the maze after entrusting his work to Grover and the others, marking the end of an age for satyrs and nature spirits. Percy returns home for his birthday, where his mother, Sally, is now happily involved with a kind mortal teacher, Paul Blofis. The gravest turn is the enemy's: the Titan lord Kronos completes his return by fully taking over the body of Luke, who has given himself to his master, so the coming war will be led by Kronos in a demigod's form. Nico di Angelo, reconciled somewhat with Percy, reveals a dangerous plan for how Percy might stand against Kronos when the final conflict comes. The great prophecy about a child of the eldest gods now points squarely toward Percy as his sixteenth birthday nears.
recaps.in_short: Percy learns that Daedalus's Labyrinth has an entrance inside Camp Half-Blood, so Luke's army could invade from within. Annabeth leads a quest, with Percy, Grover, and Tyson, into the maze to reach the inventor Daedalus before the enemy can obtain the means to control it. In the shifting maze they meet gods and monsters, cross paths with Nico, a son of Hades shadowed by a manipulative ghost, and seek Hephaestus, who sends Percy into a volcano. Blown clear, Percy washes up on Calypso's island before choosing to leave and is found to have been presumed dead. The mortal Rachel Elizabeth Dare, who sees through the Mist, guides them to Daedalus, who has been living at camp as the instructor Quintus. Grover finds the dying wild god Pan, who passes on his work. When Luke's army invades through the maze, Daedalus dies to collapse it, and the camp holds. Kronos completes his return by taking over Luke's body, and Nico shares a plan for the war ahead.

recaps.text: Previously: Percy Jackson, demigod son of Poseidon, trained at Camp Half-Blood with his friends Annabeth, a daughter of Athena, and Grover, a satyr, and gained a Cyclops half-brother, Tyson. His old camp friend Luke betrayed the gods to serve the reviving Titan lord Kronos. On a quest west, Percy helped free the goddess Artemis and trap the Titan Atlas beneath the sky, but lost the Hunter Zoe and a young half-blood, Bianca di Angelo. Bianca's brother, Nico, blaming Percy for her death, fled and revealed himself as a son of Hades, able to command the dead. Thalia, a daughter of Zeus, joined the Hunters, leaving a prophecy about a child of the eldest gods pointing toward Percy as war with the Titans looms.

At high school orientation, Percy is helped by a mortal girl, Rachel Elizabeth Dare, who can see through the Mist, and fights off demon attackers before fleeing to camp. There a new sword instructor named Quintus has appeared with a friendly hellhound, and Percy and Annabeth discover that an entrance to Daedalus's Labyrinth, the ancient maze, lies within the camp's borders, meaning the enemy could invade from within. Percy also witnesses Nico, now a son of Hades who can raise the dead, being guided by a scheming ghost toward a bargain to restore his sister. To keep the enemy from mastering the maze, a quest is given to Annabeth to find Daedalus first.

Annabeth leads Percy, Grover, and Tyson into the ever-shifting Labyrinth. Inside they meet gods and monsters, free an ancient hundred-handed creature whom Tyson befriends, and again cross paths with Nico, who is pursuing his own grim errand. They defeat a three-bodied giant on his ranch and seek out the smith-god Hephaestus for guidance. Hephaestus agrees to help only if Percy first investigates who has been intruding on one of his volcano forges, sending Percy off toward a dangerous confrontation while the others continue searching for the inventor.

Investigating the forge beneath a mountain, Percy unleashes a burst of destructive power against the enemy's servants and is thrown clear as the volcano erupts. He washes up on the hidden island of the nymph Calypso, who heals him and offers him a peaceful life there, but he chooses to leave and return to his friends. Percy discovers he was gone long enough to be presumed dead. Needing a guide who can navigate the deceptive maze by sight, the questers bring in the mortal Rachel, whose clear vision can lead them where magic misleads.

Guided by Rachel through the maze, the group reaches the workshop of Daedalus and learns that the inventor, kept alive for ages by moving his mind into automaton bodies, has been living at camp disguised as Quintus. He holds the key to controlling the Labyrinth that both sides want. Meanwhile Grover at last finds the lost wild god Pan, deep within the maze. Pan is fading as the world's wild places dwindle; at peace, he entrusts his work to Grover and the others before dying, ending an age for satyrs and nature spirits.

Luke's Titan army invades Camp Half-Blood through the Labyrinth. In the battle the defenders hold at a cost, and Daedalus, choosing to end his long life, dies in a way that collapses the maze and permanently closes the enemy's shortcut into the camp. The gravest development is the enemy's: the Titan lord Kronos completes his return by fully taking over the body of Luke, who has surrendered himself to his master, so the coming war will be led by Kronos wearing a demigod's form. Percy goes home for his birthday to find his mother happily involved with a kind mortal teacher, and Nico shares with him a dangerous plan for how he might stand against Kronos when the final war arrives.

characters.description: Lord of Lesnaya Zemlya, a boyar whose lands lie far north of Moscow at the edge of deep forest. A careful, hard-working man who married into the Grand Prince's family and has kept his people fed through bad winters by paying close attention to his fields, his horses and his household. He is fond of his children in an undemonstrative way and expects them to take the places the world has laid out for them.
characters.name: Pyotr Vladimirovich

characters.description: Pyotr's wife and the mother of his children, a daughter of the Grand Prince's house in Moscow. Her own mother was a woman who walked out of the forest, married a prince, bore one daughter and was never satisfactorily explained; Moscow decided she had been a witch. Marina is quiet and watchful and knows she inherited a little of whatever that was. As the book opens she is pregnant again, certain that this child will be a daughter who inherits far more than she did, and equally certain that bearing her will be her own death.
characters.name: Marina Ivanovna

characters.description: The old nurse of Pyotr's household, who came north with Marina and has raised all of her children. She tells them the winter tales by the oven, among them the story of Frost, the cold-demon of the forest, and the girl whose stepmother sent her out into the snow. Practical, devout and superstitious in equal measure, she still leaves bread out for the spirits of house and byre while crossing herself, and she knows more about where Marina's family came from than she cares to say.
characters.name: Dunya

characters.description: Pyotr's eldest son and his heir, blunt, hot-tempered and thoroughly practical, more interested in his father's land, horses and quarrels than in anything his youngest sister has to say.
characters.name: Nikolai Petrovich

characters.description: Pyotr's second son, good with horses and weapons and closer to his sisters than his elder brother is. He is also drawn towards God in a way his father finds inconvenient in a boy who is supposed to inherit land and marry well.
characters.name: Aleksandr Petrovich

characters.description: Pyotr's elder daughter: gentle, sensible and entirely conventional, the one of Marina's children who wants exactly the life she was born to have, with a good marriage, a warm house and children of her own. She is fond of her youngest sister and is often the only person in the household who can manage her.
characters.name: Olga Petrovna

characters.description: The youngest child of Pyotr Vladimirovich, born in his household in the northern forests of Rus' at the cost of her mother's life. Marina carried her deliberately, wanting a daughter who might inherit the sight her own mother had. Vasya grows up plain, restless and half-wild, happier in the woods and the stable than in the women's rooms, and unwilling to be shaped into anybody's wife. She sees what nobody else on her father's lands can see: the spirit that lives in the oven, the one in the stable, others in the water and the trees. She talks to them and feeds them and takes them entirely for granted, long before she understands what it will cost to be the only person who does.
characters.name: Vasilisa Petrovna

characters.description: Pyotr's youngest son and the sibling nearest Vasya in age, and so her companion in most of what she gets up to as a child. Steady, unimaginative and stubbornly loyal, he is the one member of the family who tends to take her word for things he cannot see himself.
characters.name: Aleksei Petrovich

characters.description: A daughter of the Grand Prince of Moscow, given in marriage to Pyotr Vladimirovich. Since childhood she has seen creatures nobody else will admit to seeing, and has concluded that she is surrounded by demons and probably damned; she wanted nothing in the world but permission to take vows and hide in a convent. Devout, frightened and brittle, she is sent instead to a household at the edge of the forest where the things she dreads live in every oven, stable and bathhouse.
characters.name: Anna Ivanovna

characters.description: The spirit of Pyotr's house, who lives in the oven and keeps the family safe from what is outside. He grows strong on the bread and porridge left out for him and thin and grey when the offerings stop. Vasya has fed him since she was small and can see and speak with him. He is her first proof that the winter tales are describing something real, and his health is a fair measure of the household's.
characters.name: The Domovoi

characters.description: A young priest sent north from Moscow: famous for the icons he paints and for a voice that can hold a congregation completely still. He is genuinely gifted and genuinely devout, and also proud, ambitious and badly stung at being posted to a village at the edge of the world rather than a great church. He finds a people who keep the fasts and also leave bread out for the spirits of house and yard, and he sets about burning the second habit out of them. Pyotr's strange younger daughter, who neither fears him nor believes him, unsettles him from the start.
characters.name: Konstantin Nikonovich

characters.description: Anna's daughter by Pyotr, and Vasya's half-sister: a sweet, timid, obedient little girl who is everything her mother hoped for and nothing like the stepdaughter her mother is afraid of. Vasya is fond of her.
characters.name: Irina Petrovna

characters.description: A water-spirit of the forest near Lesnaya Zemlya, a drowned-looking woman who lives by a lake and an old oak. She takes an interest in Vasya, combs her hair, and begins teaching her what a girl who can see is able to do. She is also candid about how badly things are going for her own kind now that the village has stopped putting out offerings.
characters.name: The Rusalka

characters.description: The frost-demon of Dunya's winter tales, who in the stories rewards a patient girl and freezes a greedy one. He turns out to be entirely real: a pale-eyed man who appears in the winter woods, and who is death as much as cold, the one who comes for people who die in the snow. He has been paying attention to Vasya's family for longer than she has been alive, and to her in particular. He does not explain himself, his gifts have costs, and he is a great deal less free than he looks.
characters.name: Morozko

characters.description: A bay stallion out of the winter-king's own herd, and not an ordinary horse: he understands what is said to him and answers, he chooses his rider rather than the other way round, and he will wear neither saddle nor bridle. His name means nightingale. He attaches himself to Vasya.
characters.name: Solovey

characters.description: The winter-king's twin and opposite: a one-eyed spirit who feeds on fear and madness and grows strongest where people are most frightened. He was bound long ago, and what has kept him bound is not only his brother's work but the small, steady habit of ordinary people leaving bread for the powers of house and forest. As that habit is preached out of them his chains slacken. He raises the dead, whispers to the devout in language they will mistake for holiness, and wants only to be loose.
characters.name: Medved

recaps.ending: The Bear is loose, the dead are walking, and Vasya rides home from the winter-king's house to find that Lesnaya Zemlya has decided she is the cause of all of it. Anna Ivanovna dies in the chaos. Konstantin learns that the voice he has obeyed and preached for was the Bear's and not God's, and has nothing left to say. In the forest clearing where the thing was first bound, Vasya faces it, and her father follows her there; because the Bear can only be chained again by a life freely surrendered, Pyotr Vladimirovich gives up his own and dies in the snow. Morozko binds his brother, and the winter finally breaks. The household survives, but Pyotr is dead, Dunya is dead, and the village wants the witch's daughter gone. Vasya refuses both of the futures her world allows her, a husband or a convent, and there is no third one. Alyosha stays to hold their father's lands. Olga is a princess in Moscow, and Sasha is a monk who does not yet know what has happened at home. Konstantin leaves for Moscow with his reputation intact and his faith in ruins. Vasya rides north and away on Solovey, wearing Morozko's blue jewel, intending to travel as far as the road goes, and carrying his warning that the world outside is no kinder than the one she is leaving.
recaps.in_short: In a lord's household in the forests north of medieval Moscow, Marina Ivanovna dies bearing a daughter she wanted deliberately, believing the child would inherit the strange sight of her own mother. Vasilisa grows up seeing the household spirits of Rus' and feeding them as her people always have. Her father remarries a devout, terrified girl from Moscow who sees the same creatures and calls them demons, and a proud young priest, Konstantin Nikonovich, is sent north and preaches the old observances away. As the offerings stop the spirits weaken, and so does the binding on a one-eyed devil called the Bear, who feeds on fear and raises the dead. Refusing marriage and the convent both, Vasya is driven out into the snow and taken in by Morozko, the frost-demon and death-god of the winter tales, who has been quietly arming her for years without saying so. She rides home on a stallion called Solovey to face the Bear, and her father dies giving up his life freely so that the Bear can be bound again. Named a witch by her own village, Vasya leaves home to see the world.

recaps.text: In a lord's household called Lesnaya Zemlya, deep in the forests north of Moscow, the old nurse Dunya tells the children winter tales by the oven, among them the story of Frost, the cold-demon who rewards a patient girl and kills a greedy one. Their mother, Marina Ivanovna, is pregnant again. Marina is a daughter of the Grand Prince's house, but her own mother was a strange woman who came out of the forest and married into Moscow, and Marina has always known she inherited a little of that strangeness. She is certain the child will be a girl who inherits far more, and just as certain that bearing her will be her own death. She insists on it anyway, over her husband Pyotr Vladimirovich's objections. She gives birth to a daughter, Vasilisa, and dies. Pyotr is left with five children, the eldest three nearly grown, the baby handed to Dunya to raise. In time he begins to think about the marriages his older children will need, and about the journey south to Moscow that arranging them will require.

Vasya grows up in the forest, plain and restless and impossible to keep indoors, and she can see things nobody else does: the small spirit in the oven, the one in the stable, others in the water and the trees. Dunya, who half believes and wholly worries, tells her to keep quiet about it. Pyotr rides south to Moscow with his elder children to settle their futures. Olga is betrothed to Vladimir Andreevich, prince of Serpukhov, a better match than her father hoped for. Sasha refuses the life planned for him and goes instead to the monastery on Makovets Hill, to take vows under the holy man Sergei. The Grand Prince offers Pyotr his own daughter, Anna Ivanovna, in marriage, an honour Pyotr is in no position to decline, although Anna herself wants nothing but a convent. In a Moscow marketplace a stranger with pale eyes presses a blue jewel on a silver chain into Pyotr's hand and says it is for his youngest daughter. Pyotr carries it north uneasily. Dunya takes one look at it, decides she knows what it is, and hides it away rather than hang it round a child's neck.

Pyotr brings Anna Ivanovna home as his wife. Anna has seen demons all her life, or believes she has, and Lesnaya Zemlya is full of them: every stable, bathhouse and oven has its occupant, and she is the only adult in the house who can see them. Discovering that her small stepdaughter sees them too, and is not remotely afraid, turns Anna's fear into hatred. Anna bears Pyotr a daughter, Irina, a quiet conventional child of the sort she understands. Olga marries and goes south, becoming a princess of Serpukhov and a fixture of Moscow's court. Sasha is lost to the monastery. Vasya, left with her father, Alyosha, Dunya and a stepmother who prays against her, goes on feeding the house-spirit in the oven and wandering further into the forest than anyone thinks safe. Dunya keeps the blue jewel hidden, and sleeps badly, because night after night the pale-eyed man who gave it appears in her dreams and tells her to hand it over.

Years pass. Vasya is nearly grown and refuses every mention of a husband. A priest arrives from Moscow: Konstantin Nikonovich, a young man with a famous voice and a rare gift for painting icons, sent north by men at court who found his ambition inconvenient. He is appalled by what he finds, a village that keeps the fasts and also leaves bread out for the spirits of house and byre, and he sets about ending the second practice. His preaching works. The offerings stop, and the effect is immediate to the one person who can see it: the house-spirit in the oven goes thin and grey, the guardians of stable and yard fade, and the old protections around Lesnaya Zemlya begin to fail. Vasya cannot make anyone believe her. Out in the forest she keeps company with a water-spirit who lives by a lake, a drowned-looking woman who combs her hair, takes an interest in her, and begins teaching her what a girl who can see is able to do.

Konstantin's hold on the village tightens, and Anna Ivanovna makes him her confessor and her ally against Vasya. A voice begins speaking to Konstantin at night, praising him, telling him what to preach and what he might yet become; he takes it for God. Winter comes early and refuses to break. The harvest was poor, the cold kills livestock and then people, and wolves come to the fences. Then the dead stop staying buried: a man laid in his grave walks back into the village at night, and the fading house-spirits can no longer keep such things out. Vasya sees exactly what is happening and fights it more or less alone; Alyosha believes her, and almost nobody else will. To Anna and Konstantin the obvious explanation for a hard winter and walking corpses is that Pyotr's strange daughter is a witch, and they press him to marry her off at once or shut her in a convent.

Worn down by the pale-eyed man in her dreams, Dunya finally gives Vasya the blue jewel she has hidden for years, and dies. Pyotr, pushed by his wife and his priest and unnerved by his own daughter, arranges a marriage for her; Vasya refuses it, and refuses the convent as well. The village is in a bad way by now, the cold unbroken, the dead abroad at night, the small powers that once guarded the household nearly gone, and the blame has settled firmly on Vasya. Driven out into the winter forest with nowhere to go, exhausted and freezing, she is found in the snow by the frost-demon of Dunya's tales.

Vasya wakes in a house among the firs that has no business existing, kept by servants who do not speak, where she is warm and fed and healing and time does not seem to move. Her host is Morozko, the winter-king of the old stories, who is frost and also death, and who has been watching her family for generations. The blue jewel is his work, made to steady and strengthen her, and he has been paying for it out of his own power. In his stable she meets a bay stallion called Solovey, who talks, chooses his own rider, and will wear neither saddle nor bridle; she learns to ride him. Morozko finally tells her what has been happening at home. Something old was bound in the forest near Lesnaya Zemlya, and the binding always depended on ordinary people going on believing in the powers of house and wood. Konstantin has preached that belief away, and the thing in the forest is very nearly loose. Vasya will not stay where it is safe. She takes Solovey and rides home.

Vasya comes home to a village convinced she is a witch and a household under siege by the dead. The thing in the forest is free: Medved, the Bear, the winter-king's one-eyed twin, who feeds on terror, has been raising the dead all winter, and whose voice Konstantin mistook for God's. Anna Ivanovna dies. Konstantin, confronted with what he has actually been serving, is left with nothing. Vasya rides to the clearing to face the Bear, and her father follows her there. The Bear can only be bound again by a life given up freely, and Pyotr Vladimirovich gives his, dying so that his daughter and his people live. Morozko chains his brother once more and the winter breaks at last. The village buries its dead and holds Vasya responsible for all of them. She will not marry and she will not take vows, and her world offers a woman no third option, so she says goodbye to Alyosha, who will hold their father's lands now, and rides away north on Solovey to see the world. Konstantin returns to Moscow. Morozko tells her the road will not be kind, and lets her go.

characters.description: The narrator, a gifted, high-achieving college student from a modest Massachusetts family, spending a summer in New York as a guest editor at a fashion magazine after winning a writing contest. Ambitious and academically brilliant, she is also increasingly detached and unhappy, unable to feel the excitement her glamorous opportunity is supposed to bring. Sharp-eyed and ironic, she watches herself and the world around her with a growing sense of numbness and dislocation.
characters.name: Esther Greenwood

characters.description: A witty, glamorous fellow guest editor from a fashionable Southern college, worldly and contemptuous of the program's rules and pieties. Bold, sardonic, and drawn to nightlife and men, she becomes a magnet for Esther, who is both fascinated and unsettled by her cynical confidence.
characters.name: Doreen

characters.description: A wholesome, cheerful fellow guest editor from the Midwest, earnest and conventional. Friendly and eager to do the right thing, she represents the sunny, well-adjusted young womanhood that Esther feels alienated from.
characters.name: Betsy

characters.description: The formidable, ambitious editor at the magazine who supervises Esther during the internship. Plain but brilliant and commanding, she takes a professional interest in Esther and presses her about her future plans, embodying a model of hard-driving female career success.
characters.name: Jay Cee

characters.description: Esther's clean-cut medical-student suitor, approved of by her family and long regarded as her natural match. Confident, conventional, and quietly self-righteous, he is revealed through Esther's memories to be a hypocrite about sexual double standards, and her disillusionment with him has soured her feelings. He is recovering from tuberculosis at a sanatorium.
characters.name: Buddy Willard

characters.description: A pleasant United Nations interpreter whom Esther is set up with during her time in New York. Courteous and cultured, he offers her a glimpse of a different kind of life, and their evening together prompts her to reflect on her expectations about men, marriage, and her own future.
characters.name: Constantin

characters.description: A wealthy, arrogant man Esther meets at a party near the end of her New York stay. Aggressive and contemptuous of women, he treats their encounter as a conquest and turns violent, an experience that darkens the close of her time in the city.
characters.name: Marco

characters.description: Esther's widowed mother, a practical, hardworking woman who teaches shorthand and typing to support the family. Anxious and well-meaning but limited in her understanding of her daughter's inner state, she urges conventional coping and worries over Esther as she returns home from New York.
characters.name: Mrs. Greenwood

characters.description: The first psychiatrist Esther is sent to after her return home. Handsome, self-satisfied, and remote, he shows little real insight into her distress, and his impersonal manner and clumsy treatment deepen rather than ease her suffering.
characters.name: Dr. Gordon

characters.description: A wealthy, elderly novelist who funded the scholarship that sent Esther to college. Generous and interested in Esther's welfare, she intervenes to pay for her care at a private hospital, offering a route to better treatment.
characters.name: Philomena Guinea

characters.description: The perceptive, sympathetic female psychiatrist who takes charge of Esther's care at the private hospital. Warm, honest, and reassuring, she wins Esther's trust and oversees a careful, humane course of treatment, becoming a steadying presence in her recovery.
characters.name: Dr. Nolan

characters.description: A young woman from Esther's hometown and college circle who had also been involved with Buddy Willard, now a fellow patient at the private hospital. Composed and even admiring toward Esther, she becomes a strange sort of double and companion during Esther's time under treatment.
characters.name: Joan Gilling

recaps.ending: Under Dr. Nolan's humane care at the private hospital, Esther slowly climbs out of her breakdown through insulin treatment and a course of properly administered electroshock that finally lifts the crushing weight of her depression. She begins to reclaim a sense of control over her own life, most pointedly by being fitted for a diaphragm and then losing her virginity to a man named Irwin, an encounter that leaves her hemorrhaging badly and needing medical help. Her fellow patient Joan Gilling, a woman from her past who had also known Buddy Willard, appears to be improving but then hangs herself, and Esther attends her funeral. As the novel closes, Esther, much recovered and released from many of her old illusions, waits to be interviewed by the hospital board before returning to college. She steps toward the door uncertain of the future and conscious that the bell jar of madness might one day close over her again, but for now free of it and ready to go on. Buddy visits and their romance is plainly over.
recaps.in_short: Esther Greenwood, a brilliant college student, spends a summer as a guest editor at a New York fashion magazine but feels numb and disconnected amid its glamour, disillusioned with the expectations placed on young women and with her conventional suitor Buddy Willard. Returning home to Massachusetts, she learns she has been rejected from a writing course and sinks into a severe depression, unable to sleep, read, or write. An incompetent psychiatrist subjects her to a traumatic electroshock treatment, and her despair deepens until she attempts suicide by swallowing sleeping pills and hiding in a crawlspace. Found alive after several days, she is hospitalized and eventually transferred, through the help of a wealthy benefactor, to a private hospital under the care of the compassionate Dr. Nolan. There, with insulin therapy and properly managed electroshock, she gradually recovers. A fellow patient and acquaintance, Joan Gilling, hangs herself, and Esther, having taken new steps toward independence, prepares to leave the hospital and resume her life, cautiously hopeful but aware that the suffocating bell jar of her illness could descend again.

recaps.text: Esther Greenwood, a talented scholarship student, has won a month in New York as one of a dozen college girls guest-editing a fashion magazine, staying at a women's hotel and swept through luncheons, photo shoots, and parties. Instead of the excitement she is supposed to feel, she is increasingly numb and estranged from it all. She is pulled between two fellow interns: the cynical, glamorous Doreen, who flouts the program's rules and chases nightlife, and the wholesome, conventional Betsy. A magazine banquet leaves the group with food poisoning, and encounters with the driven editor Jay Cee and a courteous United Nations interpreter push Esther to brood on her future and on what a woman is expected to want. Threaded through these New York days are her memories of her medical-student suitor Buddy Willard, whose hypocrisy about sex and smug conventionality have soured her on him and on the settled married life he represents, deepening her sense that she does not fit the roles laid out for her.

Esther's New York month ends bleakly, and she returns home to the Boston suburbs only to learn she has been rejected from a summer writing course she was counting on. With the structure of her ambitions knocked away, she spirals into a deepening depression: she cannot sleep, cannot read or write, and stops washing or changing her clothes, while her anxious mother urges ordinary cheer she cannot summon. Sent to the complacent psychiatrist Dr. Gordon, she is given a badly handled electroshock treatment that terrifies and further isolates her. Her thoughts turn obsessively to death, and she circles various methods before finally swallowing a bottle of sleeping pills and crawling into a hidden space beneath the house. She is discovered still alive after several days and hospitalized. Through the intervention of the wealthy novelist Philomena Guinea, who once funded her scholarship, she is moved to a private hospital, where the sympathetic Dr. Nolan takes charge of her care and a more humane course of treatment begins.

At the private hospital, under Dr. Nolan's steady and compassionate guidance, Esther slowly recovers through insulin therapy and, crucially, a course of properly administered electroshock that at last lifts the smothering weight of her depression. She regains a foothold in reality and begins to assert control over her own life, including being fitted for a diaphragm as a step toward independence and then losing her virginity to a mathematics professor named Irwin, an encounter that leaves her bleeding dangerously and needing to be rushed for help. A fellow patient, Joan Gilling, a young woman from Esther's hometown who had also been tied to Buddy Willard, seems to be getting better but then hangs herself, and Esther goes to her funeral. Buddy visits, and it is clear their relationship is finished. As the book ends, Esther, greatly improved and stripped of many old illusions, waits to be interviewed by the hospital board before leaving to resume her studies. She walks toward the meeting uncertain but alive and hopeful, aware that the bell jar that once sealed her off could someday descend again, yet for now released from it.

characters.description: An LAPD homicide detective in Hollywood Division whose refusal to accept convenient answers repeatedly puts him at odds with his superiors. A former Army tunnel soldier in Vietnam, he recognizes the dead man found in a drainage pipe as someone from that buried part of his life.
characters.name: Harry Bosch

characters.description: The man found dead near Mulholland Dam. He served with Bosch as a tunnel soldier in Vietnam and later struggled with heroin, making an overdose seem plausible until details at the scene trouble Bosch.
characters.name: Billy Meadows

characters.description: Bosch's partner in Hollywood homicide. He is sociable, ambitious, and more willing than Bosch to accommodate department expectations, though he continues helping with the Meadows investigation.
characters.name: Jerry Edgar

characters.description: The lieutenant commanding Bosch's squad. He is primarily concerned with orderly case management and with keeping Bosch from creating another public problem for the department.
characters.name: Harvey Pounds

characters.description: A senior LAPD official who monitors Bosch closely and protects the department's institutional interests. He is stern, politically alert, and unwilling to let Bosch define the limits of his own investigation.
characters.name: Irvin Irving

characters.description: An FBI agent assigned to the bank-robbery squad. Methodical and self-contained, she becomes Bosch's principal federal counterpart when the Meadows death intersects with an unsolved tunnel burglary.
characters.name: Eleanor Wish

characters.description: An experienced FBI agent working with Eleanor Wish on the tunnel-burglary investigation. He understands the Bureau's evidence and procedures and regards Bosch's independent methods with caution.
characters.name: John Rourke

characters.description: An Internal Affairs detective assigned to watch Bosch. Lewis treats the surveillance as an opportunity to catch Bosch breaking rules rather than as a neutral inquiry.
characters.name: Lewis

characters.description: Lewis's Internal Affairs partner. He helps maintain the covert watch on Bosch while the homicide detective pursues the Meadows case.
characters.name: Clarke

characters.description: A teenage street hustler who was near the reservoir on the night Meadows died. His shifting account makes him both a possible witness and a vulnerable link in the investigation.
characters.name: Sharkey

recaps.ending: Bosch and Wish enter the storm-drain system as the burglary plan reaches its end. FBI agent John Rourke is exposed as the insider who directed the operation and eliminated people who could connect him to it, including Billy Meadows. Rourke tries to kill Bosch underground but dies during the confrontation. Wish then admits that she knowingly took part in the scheme: the targeted vault held valuables tied to men she blamed for her brother's death in Vietnam, and her alliance with Bosch did not erase her role in the crimes. She surrenders and is imprisoned. Bosch solves Meadows's murder and survives both the tunnel and Internal Affairs scrutiny, but the relationship he had begun with Wish ends with her confession. The case leaves him facing the cost of pursuing truth when the people closest to the investigation have concealed the most important facts.
recaps.in_short: A body in a drainage pipe draws LAPD detective Harry Bosch back to his service as a Vietnam tunnel soldier when he identifies the dead man as former comrade Billy Meadows. Signs that the apparent overdose was staged connect the death to a sophisticated bank-vault burglary carried out through Los Angeles tunnels. Bosch works uneasily with FBI agent Eleanor Wish while Internal Affairs watches him and more witnesses are placed in danger. The inquiry moves from veterans of the tunnel units to the people who knew confidential details of the robbery investigation. Bosch ultimately enters the underground route and breaks up a second operation. He learns that trusted participants on the investigative side helped plan the crimes and silence Meadows. One dies in the confrontation; another confesses and goes to prison. The murder is solved, but Bosch's growing personal attachment to Wish is destroyed by the truth.

recaps.text: Harry Bosch is called to a body in a drainage pipe near Mulholland Dam. Patrol officers assume the dead man overdosed, but Bosch notices signs that the scene has been arranged. He recognizes the victim as Billy Meadows, a fellow member of a Vietnam tunnel unit who later became addicted to heroin. The personal connection gives Bosch another reason to resist pressure for a quick disposition. As he and Jerry Edgar trace Meadows's last movements, Bosch learns that the dead man had recently possessed more money than his circumstances explained. His superiors, including Lieutenant Harvey Pounds and Irvin Irving, are already wary of Bosch's methods, while Internal Affairs detectives Lewis and Clarke begin covertly following him. What looks like a routine drug death becomes a homicide inquiry tied to Bosch's own past.

Evidence around Meadows points toward an earlier burglary in which thieves tunneled into a bank and opened selected safe-deposit boxes. Because the method resembles military tunnel work, Bosch sees a possible role for veterans with Meadows's training. The federal bank-robbery squad, represented by Eleanor Wish and John Rourke, protects its investigation and initially resists Bosch's intrusion. Bosch and Wish nevertheless begin comparing the homicide evidence with the still-unsolved theft. A teenager called Sharkey may have seen activity near the place where Meadows was left, but he is frightened and unreliable. The parallel police and FBI inquiries now share suspects, methods, and an underground geography.

Bosch and Wish follow the connections among Meadows, other former tunnel soldiers, and the bank job. Technical details show that the thieves understood both underground construction and the authorities' response. Bosch's refusal to stay within departmental boundaries intensifies the Internal Affairs surveillance. He and Wish also grow personally close, although each continues holding back parts of the past. Sharkey's knowledge makes him increasingly exposed; when he is killed, the case demonstrates that the people behind the tunnel operation are still active and willing to remove witnesses. Bosch concludes that the original burglary was not an isolated event and begins looking for the next target.

The investigation narrows around a fresh underground route and valuables held in another secured location. Bosch uses what he remembers from Vietnam to understand how the team will move, ventilate its passage, and control anyone who reaches it. The killers appear to know investigative information that should be confined to law enforcement, forcing Bosch to consider an insider without yet knowing where the breach lies. Lewis and Clarke's surveillance complicates his movements and creates a second danger around the operation.
