Bosch and Wish prepare to enter the tunnels rather than wait for the thieves to emerge, aware that the enclosed space favors people trained for it.

Bosch and Wish move toward the active tunnel as the robbery team puts its plan into motion. The route, equipment, and timing confirm that Meadows was part of a practiced group and that his death followed a breakdown in trust among its members. Above ground, the overlapping LAPD, FBI, and Internal Affairs operations create confusion about who has reliable information. Underground, Bosch is forced to rely on skills he had hoped to leave in Vietnam. The case has become a contest over who can reach the vault and escape route first, while the identity of the person directing the thieves remains unresolved.

Inside the tunnel system, Bosch discovers that FBI agent John Rourke has been directing the burglary conspiracy and killing participants who threatened to expose it, including Billy Meadows. Rourke attempts to eliminate Bosch but dies in the underground confrontation, ending the immediate operation. Eleanor Wish then reveals her own knowing part in the scheme. Her motive was bound to her brother's death in Vietnam and to the valuables selected from the vault, but she accepts that this does not excuse the crimes. Wish surrenders and is sent to prison. Bosch closes Meadows's murder and emerges from the Internal Affairs pressure, yet his trust in Wish and the relationship developing between them are finished. The epilogue leaves him alive and vindicated on the case, but isolated by what solving it required him to learn.

characters.description: An LAPD homicide detective in Hollywood Division, still known for pursuing cases beyond the limits set by his supervisors. When a narcotics officer's death is quickly labeled suicide, Bosch sees inconsistencies and begins an inquiry he has not been assigned.
characters.name: Harry Bosch

characters.description: An LAPD narcotics detective found dead in a motel room, apparently by his own hand. His work concerned the drug called black ice, and his final message suggests that he had uncovered something about his own origins.
characters.name: Calexico Moore

characters.description: Cal Moore's widow, a teacher who had become separated from her husband before his death. She gives Bosch a view of Cal outside police work and wants an honest account of what happened to him.
characters.name: Sylvia Moore

characters.description: Bosch's lieutenant in Hollywood Division. Pounds insists on assignments, clearance rates, and chain of command, all of which Bosch disregards when he takes an interest in Moore's death.
characters.name: Harvey Pounds

characters.description: A senior LAPD official focused on controlling the institutional risk created by a dead narcotics officer. He expects Bosch to observe departmental boundaries and reacts strongly when Bosch does not.
characters.name: Irvin Irving

characters.description: Bosch's regular homicide partner. Edgar assists when available but is less willing to jeopardize his position for a case their squad does not officially own.
characters.name: Jerry Edgar

characters.description: A deputy medical examiner whose findings help Bosch test the official account of Cal Moore's death. She is direct about the physical evidence and resistant to pressure to make it say more than it can.
characters.name: Teresa Corazon

characters.description: A homicide detective approaching retirement whose neglected case load includes a dead man with links to the black-ice trade. His records give Bosch a route from Los Angeles street deaths toward the supply chain.
characters.name: Lucius Porter

characters.description: The powerful trafficker known as the Pope, associated with the Mexican source of black ice. His secluded operation and uncertain personal history become central to Bosch's attempt to understand Moore's investigation.
characters.name: Humberto Zorrillo

characters.description: A Mexican police officer who becomes Bosch's official guide and uneasy counterpart south of the border. He knows the local balance of authority around the drug operation and the risks of challenging it.
characters.name: Aguila

recaps.ending: At the Mexican drug compound, Bosch discovers that the dead man in the motel was Humberto Zorrillo, not Cal Moore. Moore and Zorrillo were half brothers, and Moore used the shotgun damage and falsified identifying evidence to exchange their identities. After killing Zorrillo, he intended to leave his police life behind and take control of the black-ice operation under his brother's name. Bosch confronts Moore at the compound; Moore is killed as the operation collapses, and the drug facility is destroyed. The result explains the misleading suicide, the message about discovering who he was, and the Los Angeles murders linked to the trade. Bosch returns with the truth rather than the official version his superiors preferred. Sylvia has to absorb that her husband planned the deception and became the man Bosch pursued. Her connection with Bosch survives the revelation and becomes the beginning of a relationship, while Bosch's unauthorized methods leave his conflict with the department unresolved.
recaps.in_short: When narcotics detective Cal Moore is found dead in a motel, the LAPD accepts an apparent suicide, but Harry Bosch notices problems with the identification and with Moore's final message. He links the death to black ice, a dangerous street drug moving into Los Angeles from Mexico, and to another homicide that his division has allowed to stagnate. Interviews with Moore's estranged widow Sylvia and a search through his childhood reveal that the detective had been investigating both the supply network and his own family history. Bosch follows the trail across the border to a fortified drug operation controlled by a trafficker called the Pope. There he learns that the motel death was an elaborate identity exchange involving two half brothers. The architect of the deception dies when Bosch confronts him, the production site is destroyed, and Bosch returns with a solution the department had tried to avoid. He and Sylvia begin a relationship after the truth about her husband is established.

recaps.text: Previously: LAPD homicide detective Harry Bosch proved that the apparent overdose of his former Vietnam comrade Billy Meadows was murder tied to a tunnel-based bank burglary. The inquiry forced him to work with FBI agent Eleanor Wish, with whom he began a relationship. In the final underground confrontation, FBI agent John Rourke was exposed as the conspiracy's leader and died; Wish admitted her own participation and went to prison. Bosch solved the case but emerged distrustful, alone, and still in conflict with superiors who regard his independence as a threat.

On Christmas night, Bosch hears that narcotics detective Calexico Moore has been found dead in a motel room with a shotgun wound and an apparent suicide message stating that he had learned who he was. Command officers move quickly to contain the case, but Bosch is troubled by the scene and by gaps in the identification. He was not assigned the investigation, yet he begins collecting details while also carrying a homicide load his division wants closed. A potent street drug known as black ice provides a possible link to Moore's narcotics work. Bosch's decision to pursue that link puts him at odds with Lieutenant Pounds and Irvin Irving almost immediately.

Bosch reviews physical evidence from Moore's death with deputy medical examiner Teresa Corazon and finds reasons not to rely on the simple suicide account. He also takes over an ignored case involving a murdered man whose death connects to the distribution of black ice. The drug appears to be moving through an organized route rather than isolated street dealing. Cal's widow Sylvia describes a marriage that had become remote and a husband preoccupied with work and questions about his past. Bosch begins to suspect that Moore's last investigation and his personal search for identity were the same journey.

Records from Cal's childhood and police career point Bosch toward the border region where Cal grew up. At the same time, the Los Angeles homicide reveals how aggressively the black-ice organization protects its route. Bosch and Sylvia grow closer as he asks painful questions about Cal, though he does not promise that the answers will leave her husband's reputation intact. The name Humberto Zorrillo, a trafficker called the Pope, emerges behind the Mexican supply operation. Similarities and connections between Zorrillo's background and Moore's history make the official account of the motel death increasingly doubtful.

Bosch travels south without the support his superiors would require and enters a jurisdiction where the Pope's organization has money, armed protection, and influence. With Aguila as his local police contact, Bosch traces the black ice toward a remote compound where the drug is produced. He now believes that Moore learned a family secret connected to Zorrillo and that someone manipulated the condition of the motel body to prevent close identification. The closer Bosch gets to the compound, the less he can rely on official channels, and his investigation becomes an attempt to reach the central figure before the evidence or witnesses disappear.

At the drug operation, Bosch finds evidence that the solution depends on the relationship between Moore and Zorrillo rather than on a routine cartel killing. The two men were half brothers, and the damaged face of the motel corpse allowed records and assumptions to substitute for a secure identification. Bosch enters the compound while authorities close on the production site. He must distinguish the dead brother from the living one and prevent the person using the Pope's identity from completing an escape. The confrontation also places Bosch beyond any protection his department might have offered.

Bosch proves that Cal Moore killed his half brother Humberto Zorrillo and placed Zorrillo's body in the motel as his own. The shotgun wound concealed the exchange, while altered identifying evidence supported the false suicide. Moore then assumed the Pope's identity and intended to take over the black-ice business, turning his search for his origins into an escape from his police life. Bosch confronts Moore at the Mexican compound, where Moore is killed and the drug operation is destroyed. Back in Los Angeles, the result resolves both the motel deception and the related homicides, even though it exposes how eagerly the department accepted a convenient answer. Sylvia learns what Cal did and begins a relationship with Bosch after the case, leaving Bosch personally less isolated but still professionally at odds with Pounds and Irving.

characters.description: A fifteen-year-old boy from Rekton, a small town in the ruined satrapy of Tyrea. Heavy, sharp-tongued and used to being the butt of the town's jokes, he lives close to destitution because his mother spends what little they have on the drug haze. He has never been told who his father is. He scavenges the old battlefield at nearby Sundered Rock, where the civil war of sixteen years ago ended, and he reacts to light in ways he does not yet have a name for.
characters.name: Kip

characters.description: The Prism: the one living person who can split light into every colour, and by doing so hold the world's magic in balance. He is the spiritual head of the Seven Satrapies and the most powerful drafter alive, sixteen years after winning the False Prism's War against his younger brother Dazen. Charming, restless and privately afraid, he has set himself five great purposes and keeps a careful count of the years he believes he has left.
characters.name: Gavin Guile

characters.description: Gavin's younger brother, dead sixteen years. When the Chromeria named Gavin the next Prism, Dazen refused to accept it, declared himself Prism instead, and split the Seven Satrapies in a civil war remembered as the False Prism's War. It ended at Sundered Rock in Tyrea, and the histories say Gavin killed him there. Tyrea has been treated as a defeated province ever since.
characters.name: Dazen Guile

characters.description: A red and green bichrome drafter and a member of the Blackguard, the elite corps sworn to protect the Prism and the White. Before the war she was betrothed to Gavin Guile. A fire at her family's estate killed several of her brothers and was blamed on his brother Dazen, and the war that followed finished the ruin of her house. She is small, fast, quick to anger, and has never entirely put down her grievance against Gavin.
characters.name: Karris White Oak

characters.description: A man held in a seamless cell of blue luxin somewhere beneath the world, fed through a slot and visited by exactly one person. He insists on his own name, keeps count of the years, and works patiently at the only project left to him: getting out.
characters.name: The prisoner

characters.description: Kip's mother, worn down by years of the drug haze and by whatever she has been running from. She is cruel to her son as often as she is affectionate, and she has kept hidden both the name of his father and an object she has never explained.
characters.name: Katalina Delauria

characters.description: Rekton's dyer, a quiet widower whose daughter is away studying at the Chromeria. The town respects him for reasons it cannot quite articulate, and he is plainly more than a provincial craftsman who happened to settle in a backwater.
characters.name: Corvan Danavis

characters.description: Aliviana Danavis, the dyer's daughter, now a yellow drafter in her final years at the Chromeria. Clever and proud, she is held on a short leash by the debts her schooling has run up and by the fact that she is Tyrean, which in the Seven Satrapies is a thing to apologise for. She knew Kip when they were children in Rekton.
characters.name: Aliviana Danavis

characters.description: The self-declared king of Tyrea and son of the satrap the Chromeria deposed at the end of the war. He is assembling an army of soldiers and unlicensed drafters and intends to take back the satrapy his family lost, starting with the towns that submitted.
characters.name: Rask Garadul

characters.description: The White: the administrative head of the Chromeria and the deliberate counterweight to the Prism. Elderly and confined to a wheeled chair, she runs the institution's politics, its money and its informants with great patience, and is entirely immune to charm.
characters.name: The White

characters.description: Commander of the Blackguard, a very large Parian officer with a shaved head and an unshakeable calm. He answers to the White and the Prism both, trains his people hard, and is one of the few men Gavin Guile treats as an equal.
characters.name: Ironfist

characters.description: Gavin's father, head of House Guile and the satrapy of Ruthgar's representative on the Spectrum, the council of Colors that governs the Chromeria alongside the White. A lifetime of drafting red has left his eyes unable to bear light, so he conducts all his business from a sealed, unlit room. He is the most dangerous political operator in the Seven Satrapies, plays the card game Nine Kings for stakes that are never really about cards, and treats his family as instruments.
characters.name: Andross Guile

characters.description: Gavin's mother and the manager of House Guile's public face and much of its private business. She is warmer to Kip than her husband is and considerably shrewder than she allows herself to appear.
characters.name: Felia Guile

characters.description: A man burned almost past recognition, his skin cracked through with seams of every colour of luxin. He takes command of the rebellion's drafters and offers them something the Chromeria never has: a future in which drafters are not put to death when their power runs out, and in which the Chromeria's authority is broken altogether.
characters.name: The Color Prince

recaps.ending: Garriston cannot be held. Gavin gets the city's people out by sea and leaves Corvan Danavis, his old general, in charge of the refugees, while the rebellion takes the ruined city. Rask Garadul is dead, killed by Kip with the jewelled dagger his mother left him, and one of the dagger's seven stones has filled with stolen colour, which nobody can yet explain. Command of the rebellion passes to the Color Prince, who intends to break the Chromeria outright. Aliviana Danavis, disgusted by how the Chromeria treats Tyrea and by the Freeing, the ritual killing of drafters who reach the end of their power, goes over to him willingly. Karris is recovered alive and knows now that Kip is a Guile. Beneath the Chromeria, the prisoner breaks out of his blue cell and finds only another cell beyond it, and at the same time Gavin loses blue for good. The last thing the book gives the reader is the truth behind all of it: the man the world calls Gavin Guile is Dazen. He won the war, took his dead-seeming brother's name, face and office, and has kept the real Gavin alive in a private prison ever since. Kip is the son of a man who does not exist, and Gavin's five great purposes and shrinking span of colours are the debts of a sixteen-year-old lie.
recaps.in_short: In the Seven Satrapies, drafters turn light into luxin, a physical substance, and pay for it with their lives; the Prism alone can draft every colour, and the Chromeria governs magic in his name. Sixteen years after Gavin Guile won a civil war against his brother Dazen, a fifteen-year-old boy named Kip watches his Tyrean town destroyed by a would-be king, receives a jewelled dagger and the claim that Gavin is his father from his dying mother, and is swept up by the Prism himself. At the Chromeria Kip meets a family that regards him as a liability, while Gavin conceals two things: that his colours are failing one by one, and that he keeps a prisoner in a cell beneath the tower. When the rebellion marches, Gavin raises a luxin wall around the city of Garriston in a week and still loses it. Kip kills the rebel king with the dagger, which drinks the man's magic; Liv Danavis defects to the rebels' new leader, the Color Prince; and the reader learns that the Prism is actually Dazen, wearing his brother's name, and that the prisoner below is the real Gavin Guile.

recaps.text: In the Seven Satrapies, magic is drafting: a drafter converts light of one colour into luxin, a physical substance with its own properties, and pays for it with their body and eventually their life. One person in each generation, the Prism, can split light into every colour, and the Chromeria on the Jasper Isles trains and governs drafters under him and under an administrator called the White. Kip, a heavy and much-mocked fifteen-year-old, lives in the Tyrean town of Rekton with a mother lost to the drug haze. Tyrea is the losing side of the False Prism's War, fought sixteen years earlier between Gavin Guile and his younger brother Dazen and ended at Sundered Rock a short walk from the town. Kip scavenges that battlefield for scraps of old luxin. Word arrives that a man calling himself King Garadul, son of Tyrea's deposed satrap, is raising an army and marching on the towns that submitted to the Chromeria. Far away on the Jaspers, Gavin Guile tests his colours each morning, as Prisms do, and finds that the count he has been keeping in private is running out faster than anyone knows.

Garadul's army reaches Rekton and burns it, killing most of the town. Kip survives. He finds his mother dying, and she presses on him a jewelled dagger she has kept hidden for years, tells him that Gavin Guile is his father, and demands that he take revenge for her. Kip is left with a knife he does not understand, a claim he cannot prove, and no home. On the Jaspers, Gavin learns that he has a son in Tyrea. He also keeps a secret that would end him: below the Chromeria, in a cell of blue luxin, sits a prisoner whom Gavin alone visits and feeds, and who has spent sixteen years planning to get out. Karris White Oak, a Blackguard who was betrothed to Gavin before the war and has never forgiven what the war cost her family, is drawn back into his orbit as he prepares to leave the Chromeria on business he will not explain to the Spectrum.

Gavin reaches the ruins of Rekton, finds Kip, and claims him as his son in front of witnesses. They are hunted by Garadul's men and by a colour wight, a drafter who has passed the limit a body can bear and remade himself in luxin; Gavin destroys it. He carries Kip away on a craft of his own invention that skims across open water faster than any ship. Kip learns that Rekton's dyer, Master Danavis, was no provincial craftsman but Gavin's general in the war, hidden in a backwater ever since, and that he has been quietly watching over Kip for years. Kip says nothing about the dagger and keeps it out of sight. Gavin, alone, confirms what he has been dreading: one of his seven colours has gone and will not come back, which by his own arithmetic gives him about five years before the rest follow.

Gavin brings Kip to the Chromeria on Little Jasper and installs him as an acknowledged Guile bastard, which pleases nobody. The Spectrum, the council of Colors that governs alongside the White, treats a Tyrean rebellion as a provincial nuisance and is far more interested in what the Prism is doing without their permission. Kip is summoned to the sealed, lightless room of his grandfather Andross Guile, who sits as Red on the Spectrum, cannot bear light after a lifetime of drafting, and conducts the family's business and the Chromeria's politics from the dark. Andross makes Kip play the card game Nine Kings and makes plain what the boy is worth to him. Kip's grandmother Felia Guile is warmer and no less calculating. Aliviana Danavis, the dyer's daughter and a yellow drafter in her final years of study, is set to look after Kip, and the two of them recognise each other from childhood.

Kip is tested and turns out to be capable of drafting more than one colour, which makes him valuable and also a problem, and he begins the miserable business of learning to draft alongside students years younger and far better prepared. Andross Guile keeps summoning him to the dark room and the card table, and every game costs Kip something. Gavin argues with the Spectrum over Tyrea and is refused the force he asks for. Liv is pulled between her loyalty to Kip, her family debts, and the patrons who own those debts. Karris is sent south as the Chromeria's envoy to the man calling himself King Garadul, a mission designed to look like diplomacy and to gather intelligence. Gavin, unable to move the Spectrum, resolves to go to Tyrea himself and to defend Garriston, the one real city left in the satrapy, with whatever he can raise.

Karris's embassy fails; Garadul takes her prisoner rather than treating with the Chromeria, and his army moves on Garriston. Gavin sails south with Kip, Ironfist and a small force, defying the Spectrum's caution, and Liv is sent to Tyrea as well on an errand of her own patrons' devising. Garriston is a broken city, still garrisoned and still resented as the place where the war was settled, with a governor who has no intention of fighting and walls that will not stand. Gavin surveys it and decides that the only way to hold it is to build something no drafter has ever built. Kip, in the middle of all this, is being trained on the run, and continues to keep the jewelled dagger secret from everyone.

Gavin raises the Brightwater Wall around Garriston out of luxin, working the whole circuit of the city in a matter of days: a feat that has no precedent and that costs him more than he admits. The city fills with refugees from the countryside and with a scratch garrison of soldiers, sailors and untrained drafters. Kip is put to work and starts to find, painfully, that he is good for something. Liv arrives in Tyrea and is confronted with the other side of the story she has been raised on: what the Chromeria did to her satrapy after the war, and what it does to its own drafters at the end of their span. Karris, still a prisoner in Garadul's camp, learns that the rebellion is no longer really Garadul's, and that something older and stranger is directing it.

The rebel army arrives before Garriston with its own drafters and a core of colour wights who have already abandoned the limits the Chromeria sets. Gavin's defence rests on the wall, on a handful of trained fighters, and on himself, and he is quietly running out of colours to spend. Liv, travelling with the rebellion, is offered a place in it and a version of the future in which drafters are not executed once their power fails, the practice the Chromeria calls the Freeing. Karris tries to escape her captivity. Kip is armed, frightened and repeatedly told to stay out of the way. Below the Chromeria, thousands of miles from any of this, the prisoner finishes the work of sixteen years and gets his hands on the seam of his cell.

The battle for Garriston is fought over the wall and then through the streets. Gavin spends himself holding the line, and the wall he built is not enough against wights and cannon together. Kip, cut off in the fighting, comes face to face with Rask Garadul and kills him with his mother's jewelled dagger; the knife does something no weapon should do, drinking the dying man's magic into one of the seven stones set in its hilt. Karris is found and freed. The city is lost regardless, and Gavin turns from defending Garriston to evacuating it, putting the population aboard every hull in the harbour while the rebellion takes the walls.

Command of the rebellion passes to the Color Prince, a man burned nearly to ruin whose skin is cracked through with every colour of luxin, and whose ambition is not Tyrea but the destruction of the Chromeria itself. Liv Danavis chooses his side, openly and by her own reasoning. Gavin gets the refugees out to sea and leaves Corvan Danavis, his general from the war, in command of them; Karris survives and now knows Kip is a Guile; Kip keeps a dagger that has begun to fill with stolen colour. Beneath the Chromeria the prisoner breaks out of the blue cell at last and finds only another cell waiting beyond it, and in the same hour Gavin loses blue permanently. And the reader is finally told what the book has been withholding: the man the world calls Gavin Guile is Dazen. He won the war, took his brother's name, face and office, and has kept the real Gavin alive in a private prison for sixteen years. The Prism is an impostor, his failing colours are the price of it, and the boy he has just claimed as a son is the son of a dead man's name.

characters.description: A hardened warrior from the far North, missing a finger, who has outlived most of the men he ever fought beside and carries the weight of it. Feared across the North for a savagery that surfaces when the fighting turns desperate, he would rather find a way to be a better man; his weary refrain is that you have to be realistic about these things. As the book opens he is alone in the mountains, hunted by the inhuman Shanka, believing his old crew dead. He can speak with the spirits of the land, a rare and fading gift, and it is a summons from a wizard that draws him out of his hard, familiar world and south into events far larger than any single feud.
characters.name: Logen Ninefingers

characters.description: Once the most dashing and arrogant swordsman in the Union, Glokta was captured in the Gurkish wars and spent two years being tortured, emerging a wreck: half his teeth gone, a ruined leg, constant pain, and a lurching walk. Now he works the other side of the table as an Inquisitor for His Majesty's Inquisition, extracting confessions from suspected traitors. His body is broken but his mind is razor-sharp, and his sardonic inner voice, forever asking why he bothers to go on at all, is one of the book's darkest pleasures. Set to investigate corruption among the merchant guilds, he keeps tugging threads that lead somewhere far more dangerous than a few smuggling charges.
characters.name: Sand dan Glokta

characters.description: A young, handsome, and thoroughly self-absorbed nobleman holding an officer's commission he has never had to earn. Jezal cares chiefly for cards, drink, and his own reflection, and is being drilled hard by his fencing master and by his friend Major West for the Contest, the Union's celebrated duelling tournament, which he sees mostly as a shortcut to glory and admiration. Lazy but not untalented, he resents the discipline even as it begins to sharpen him. His comfortable, shallow world starts to complicate when he finds himself drawn to a sharp-tongued young woman well below his station.
characters.name: Jezal dan Luthar

characters.description: A rare thing among the Union officer class: a man of common birth who rose on merit and courage in the Gurkish wars rather than on a family name. Steady, competent, and well-liked, West coaches young Jezal for the Contest and moves uneasily between the drawing rooms of his highborn friends and his own humbler origins. Beneath the calm, though, runs a temper he works hard to master, and a fierce protectiveness toward his younger sister, Ardee, that will be tested.
characters.name: Collem West

characters.description: Major West's younger sister, newly come to the capital. Clever, well-read, and blisteringly quick with her tongue, she has little patience for the polite fictions of high society and even less for being told how to behave. She drinks more than is thought proper and enjoys unsettling the men who underestimate her. Her sparring flirtation with the vain young officer Jezal dan Luthar is one of the few honest-seeming things in the city, though it sits badly with her protective brother.
characters.name: Ardee West

characters.description: A bald, stocky old man with a short temper and a scholar's manner who arrives in the capital claiming to be Bayaz, First of the Magi, a legendary figure most educated people assume is a myth. He demands the seat on the ruling Closed Council that ancient law reserves for his order, to the fury of the men who actually run the Union. Whether he is truly the centuries-old wizard of the histories or a very convincing fraud is an open question, but power of some kind plainly moves around him, and he begins quietly gathering an unlikely handful of people for a purpose he keeps to himself.
characters.name: Bayaz

characters.description: An escaped slave out of the southern empire of Gurkhul, consumed by a single hard purpose: revenge on the people who enslaved and used her. Fierce, mistrustful, and quick to violence, she works alone and expects betrayal from everyone. When the wandering magus Yulwei takes an interest in her, it is because there is something unnatural about her; she has been touched by a power she does not understand and cannot be tracked by those hunting her in the ordinary way. He steers her, reluctant and snarling, north toward the schemes of his old master.
characters.name: Ferro Maljinn

characters.description: A Northman scout with a sharp nose and a wry, watchful nature, one of the small band of hard men who once ran with Logen Ninefingers and survived the wars that scattered them. Believing their old chief dead, the Dogman and his companions - the level-headed Rudd Threetrees, the giant Tul Duru, the near-silent bowman Grim, and the vicious Black Dow - pick their way through a North falling under the iron rule of the self-made King Bethod, looking for a way to keep breathing and, perhaps, for the friend they lost.
characters.name: The Dogman

characters.description: The cold, elegant head of His Majesty's Inquisition and one of the most powerful men in the Union. Sult presides on the Closed Council with an eye always on his rivals, and he uses Glokta as a tool, pointing him at enemies and expecting results without much caring how they are got. Ruthless and patient, he regards the state as his to defend and to steer, and treats the arrival of a meddling old man claiming ancient authority as an intolerable threat.
characters.name: Arch Lector Sult

recaps.ending: The Blade Itself ends by launching three separate journeys rather than resolving anything. Bayaz has assembled his company - Logen, Ferro, Jezal, the apprentice Malacus Quai and the Navigator Brother Longfoot - and led them out of Adua on a quest west to the edge of the World for the Seed, an ancient weapon he claims can defeat the Gurkish; the travellers are bound to him more by circumstance than by trust. Glokta has been made Superior of Dagoska by Arch Lector Sult and dispatched to the Union's crumbling southern city, tasked with holding it against an imminent Gurkish siege and with discovering what became of the predecessor who disappeared. Major Collem West has joined the Union army heading north to fight King Bethod under the incompetent Crown Prince Ladisla, leaving his sister Ardee in Glokta's keeping. Jezal, newly famous as Contest champion, leaves Ardee behind with real regret. War with the North is certain and war with the South is looming, Bayaz's true nature and intentions remain hidden, and none of the men he has set in motion can see where he means to take them. Everything is arranged; nothing is yet decided.
recaps.in_short: Three men in the declining Union - the Northman Logen Ninefingers, the self-loathing crippled Inquisitor Glokta, and the vain young officer Jezal dan Luthar - are drawn into the orbit of Bayaz, First of the Magi, an old wizard most people took for a legend. While Glokta tortures confessions out of corrupt merchants and is steered by the Arch Lector toward ever more dangerous secrets, and Jezal trains for and wins the great fencing Contest, Bayaz forces his way onto the Union's ruling council and reveals a purpose: a journey to the edge of the World to recover an ancient weapon, the Seed, to save the Union from the Gurkish Empire. By the end he has bound Logen, Jezal, the vengeful escaped slave Ferro Maljinn and others to that quest, and they set out. Glokta is sent south to hold the doomed fortress-city of Dagoska, and Major West marches north with the Union's army to war against King Bethod. Little is resolved; every road is only beginning.

recaps.text: The Union, a fading empire ruled from the great city of Adua, is introduced through three men whose lives have not yet crossed. In the far North, the scarred warrior Logen Ninefingers is ambushed by the inhuman Shanka, is separated from his companions and left believing them dead, and survives a fall into an icy river. Guided by messages from the spirits, he turns south, drawn by a summons he does not understand, and takes up with a half-frozen apprentice, Malacus Quai. In Adua, the crippled Inquisitor Sand dan Glokta - once a famous swordsman, now a torturer who despises himself - is set by his superiors to break confessions out of the Mercers, the powerful merchants' guild, and begins pulling at threads of corruption that lead higher than he was meant to reach. And the vain, idle young officer Jezal dan Luthar trains without enthusiasm for the great fencing Contest under the demanding Lord Marshal Varuz and his friend Major Collem West, while growing interested in West's sharp-tongued, hard-drinking sister, Ardee. In the North, the Dogman and the remnants of Logen's old crew, believing their chief dead, band together to survive under the tyranny of King Bethod.

Glokta's investigation into the Mercers widens into arrests and confessions, and it becomes plain that powerful men want certain questions left unasked; his master, Arch Lector Sult, steers him toward ever more dangerous targets while withholding his true purpose. Into the city walks a bald old man calling himself Bayaz, First of the Magi, who demands the ancient seat his order is owed on the ruling Closed Council. Almost no one believes he is who he claims, and his arrival unsettles the King's ministers, who had assumed the Magi were a legend. He is attended by Quai and, in time, by the boastful Navigator Brother Longfoot. Far to the south, the escaped Gurkish slave Ferro Maljinn, consumed by hatred for the Empire that enslaved her, is hunted across the desert and taken up by the wandering magus Yulwei, who senses something unnatural in her and turns her northward toward Adua. In the North, the Dogman's crew - Threetrees, Tul Duru, Black Dow, Grim and the rest - scrape a living in Bethod's shadow and begin moving toward the Union, carrying warning of the war the North is about to bring south.

Logen reaches Adua and finds himself, to his own bewilderment, taken into Bayaz's strange household, treated by the magus as a useful man rather than a savage. Bayaz forces the Closed Council to reckon with him, demonstrating a flash of real and frightening power to men who had dismissed him. Jezal, hardened by Varuz's brutal training and sharpened by his feelings for Ardee, fights his way through the rounds of the great Contest and wins it, defeating the hulking Bremer dan Gorst in the final and becoming, overnight, a celebrated man. Glokta, having survived the fallout of the Mercer affair, is handed new and more perilous work by Sult and Superior Goyle, drawn deeper into the secret rivalries of the Inquisition and the Closed Council. Across the Union the mood darkens: King Bethod's demands press on the northern border and war is all but certain, while in the South the Gurkish Empire and its Prophet, Khalul, are stirring toward a reckoning of their own. Bayaz, meanwhile, keeps his real intentions to himself, gathering the pieces he means to use.

At the book's close the scattered threads knot into a single design. Bayaz gathers his chosen company - Logen, Ferro, Jezal, the apprentice Quai and the Navigator Longfoot - and binds them to a long journey west, out past the edge of the map, to recover an ancient weapon left over from the Old Time: the Seed, which he insists is the only thing that can turn back the Gurkish. None of them fully trusts him, and Jezal in particular goes unwillingly, but each is caught up and carried along. The company leaves Adua and sets out into the ruined lands beyond the Union. At the same time the Union prepares for war on two fronts. Arch Lector Sult appoints Glokta Superior of Dagoska, the Union's isolated southern fortress-city, and sends him south to hold it against the gathering Gurkish - a posting from which his predecessor simply vanished. Major West is assigned to the army marching north to fight Bethod under the command of the vain Crown Prince Ladisla, and before he goes he asks Glokta to watch over his sister Ardee, whom Jezal is leaving behind. The three men who opened the book estranged now stand at the start of three separate roads - a quest, a siege, and a war - with Bayaz alone knowing where any of them truly lead.

characters.description: The acknowledged bastard son of the Prism, sixteen years old, heavy, self-mocking and quietly furious about most of it. He survived the destruction of his home town and the fall of Garriston, he can draft more colours than almost anyone his age, and he carries a jewelled dagger his mother left him that drank the magic of the man he killed with it. At the Chromeria he is a Guile without any of a Guile's training, watched by a grandfather who regards him as a mistake to be managed.
characters.name: Kip

characters.description: The Prism, and in truth Dazen Guile wearing his dead brother's name, face and office since he won the False Prism's War sixteen years ago. He is losing his colours one at a time, faster than he can hide, and each loss is tied to the prisoner he keeps below the Chromeria. Having failed to hold Garriston, he returns to a Chromeria that blames him for the loss and to a war he cannot fight for much longer.
characters.name: Gavin Guile

characters.description: The real Gavin Guile, held for sixteen years in a set of nested cells of coloured luxin beneath the Chromeria by the brother who took his name. He has broken out of the blue cell and found another one waiting, and he is already working on that one. Every cell he breaks costs the false Gavin the matching colour.
characters.name: The prisoner

characters.description: A red and green bichrome and a Blackguard, back at the Chromeria after captivity in Tyrea and the retreat from Garriston. Her old betrothal to Gavin is unfinished business for both of them, and she is now one of the very few people whose loyalty he has actually earned. Her family, the White Oaks, are nearly extinct and remain a piece on Andross Guile's board.
characters.name: Karris White Oak

characters.description: The head of House Guile and the Spectrum's Red, running the Chromeria's politics from a sealed dark room. He uses the card game Nine Kings as an interrogation, a lesson and a trap at once, and he wants Kip either useful or gone. He collects rare things, including the Nine Kings cards themselves, and he has never explained why.
characters.name: Andross Guile

characters.description: The White, head of the Chromeria's administration, ageing and visibly failing, still the shrewdest political mind on the Jaspers and Andross Guile's only real counterweight. She runs her own informants and has begun looking hard at who will come after her.
characters.name: The White

characters.description: Gavin's mother, still managing House Guile's respectable face while her husband works in the dark. She is near the end of her span as a drafter and knows it, and she knows a great deal about her family that she has never said aloud.
characters.name: Felia Guile

characters.description: Aliviana Danavis, formerly a Chromeria student, now travelling with the rebellion by her own choice. She has accepted the Color Prince's argument that the Chromeria's rule and its ritual killing of spent drafters are worth destroying, and she is learning what her own colour can do without the limits she was taught.
characters.name: Aliviana Danavis

characters.description: The burned man who took over the Tyrean rebellion, whose skin is seamed with every colour of luxin and who now leads an army north out of the ruins of Garriston. He preaches that drafters should be free to become whatever their magic makes of them, and that the Chromeria is the only thing standing in the way.
characters.name: The Color Prince

characters.description: Commander of the Blackguard, whose people are being asked to guard a Prism the Spectrum no longer trusts while running a class of raw recruits through the worst training on the Jaspers. He is fair, immovable, and increasingly caught between the offices he serves.
characters.name: Ironfist

characters.description: A Blackguard and Ironfist's brother, put in charge of hammering the new recruits into shape. Scarred, exacting and unnervingly quiet, he carries a reputation from the war that the recruits only hear in fragments.
characters.name: Tremblefist

characters.description: Adrasteia, a slave girl competing for one of the few open Blackguard places, which would buy her freedom. Small, fast and deliberately unremarkable, she is hiding what she can actually do: she drafts paryl, a colour below the visible spectrum that the Chromeria does not teach and mostly refuses to admit exists.
characters.name: Teia

characters.description: The outstanding recruit of Kip's class and its natural leader: disciplined, fast, and sincerely devoted to what the Blackguard is supposed to be. He decides early that Kip is worth defending and does not change his mind.
characters.name: Cruxer

characters.description: A recruit in Kip's class who drafts more than one colour and would rather build things than fight. He makes his own spectacles and gadgets and is the squad's engineer long before anyone gives him the title.
characters.name: Ben-hadad

characters.description: A recruit in Kip's class, an enthusiastic grappler with no sense of tact and an unexpected ability to blurt out the one thing nobody else has noticed.
characters.name: Ferkudi

characters.description: A young red drafter attached to the rebellion, handsome, charming and entirely without conscience. He attaches himself to Liv, and it becomes clear quickly that he is dangerous to everyone around him, including his own side.
characters.name: Zymun

characters.description: A pirate cannoneer of enormous and erratic talent, obsessed with his guns and with his own legend, who has crossed the Prism's path before and holds a grudge about it.
characters.name: Gunner

recaps.ending: Gavin marries Karris in defiance of his father's plans for a more profitable match, then sails to meet the rebellion. In the fighting around Ru he destroys the bane, the great floating body of luxin the rebellion had been growing so that an old god could be born back into the world. It costs him everything: when it is over his drafting is gone, and the Prism who could split light into seven colours cannot make one. Half-drowned and unrecognised, he is fished out of the water by the pirate cannoneer Gunner, who keeps him. The Seven Satrapies are left believing their Prism is dead, with a war they are losing, an Andross Guile free to fill the vacancy, and a Chromeria whose next Prism will have to come from somewhere. Karris is a Guile by marriage and a widow by every report she is given. Kip survives, blooded and increasingly unwilling to be managed, and now knows what the jewelled dagger is and roughly what his grandfather wants it for. Liv has gone further into the rebellion than she can walk back from. Below the Chromeria, the real Gavin Guile breaks out of another cell, and another of his brother's colours goes with it.
recaps.in_short: Garriston is lost and the Chromeria blames its Prism. While the Color Prince's army marches north out of Tyrea, Kip fights his way through Blackguard training, makes a squad out of the other misfits, and is played against his grandfather Andross across a card table that is never really about cards. The jewelled dagger Kip carries turns out to be an artifact old enough to predate the Chromeria: a knife that can strip a drafter of their magic. Gavin, secretly the brother who stole the Prism's name, loses colours faster than he can conceal, holds the Spectrum together with bluff, and buries his own mother at the ritual that kills drafters at the end of their span. He marries Karris against his father's wishes and sails to fight the rebellion at Ru, where he destroys the vast floating bane of luxin that would have birthed an old god. The victory takes his drafting entirely, and he is pulled from the sea by the pirate Gunner. The satrapies are told their Prism is dead; below the Chromeria, the real Gavin Guile breaks through another wall of his prison.

recaps.text: Previously: in the Seven Satrapies, drafters turn light into luxin and burn out their lives doing it; the Prism alone drafts every colour, and the Chromeria governs magic in his name under an administrator called the White. Sixteen years ago Gavin Guile beat his brother Dazen in the False Prism's War. Kip, a fifteen-year-old from the Tyrean town of Rekton, lost his home and his mother to a rebel king's army, and was left a jewelled dagger and the claim that Gavin Guile was his father. Gavin collected him and installed him at the Chromeria under the cold eye of Andross Guile, head of the family and the Spectrum's Red. When the rebellion marched, Gavin raised a wall of luxin around Garriston in days and still lost the city; he evacuated its people and left them with his old general Corvan Danavis. Kip killed the rebel king with the dagger, which drank the man's magic into one of its seven stones. Liv Danavis went over to the rebellion's new leader, the Color Prince. Two things the world does not know: the man who calls himself Gavin is really Dazen, who took his brother's name and face after the war, and the real Gavin has been alive the whole time in a prison beneath the Chromeria, breaking out of one coloured cell into the next. Each cell he breaks costs the false Prism that colour, and blue is already gone.

The refugees from Garriston are landed on the Jaspers and become somebody else's problem, and the Spectrum sets about blaming Gavin for the loss of a city they refused to help him defend. He returns to a Chromeria where his authority is thinner than it has ever been, his colours are still failing, and the prisoner below has already begun work on the next cell. Kip, now an acknowledged Guile with no standing, is entered for the Blackguard's open trials, the annual scramble in which a few dozen candidates fight for a handful of places. He is heavier, slower and worse trained than everyone he is up against. Andross Guile summons him back to the dark room, and it is made clear that the card game is the price of being tolerated at all.

Kip survives the trials and the training that follows, and the class of recruits sorts itself into squads. He ends up attached to a group of misfits and standouts: Cruxer, the best of them and the one who decides Kip is worth backing; Ben-hadad, who builds things; Ferkudi, who says whatever occurs to him; and Teia, a slave girl for whom a Blackguard place means freedom and who is concealing a talent the Chromeria does not teach. Tremblefist, Ironfist's scarred brother, runs them into the ground. Karris is back on duty and back within reach of Gavin, and neither of them handles it well. Andross keeps Kip at the card table and keeps winning.

The Color Prince's army moves north out of Tyrea toward Atash, gathering wights and unlicensed drafters as it goes, and the Chromeria's answer is committees. Gavin can no longer draft blue at all and is concealing how much else is going. Liv, travelling with the rebellion, is given work that suits her superviolet and pushed to see how far past the Chromeria's limits a drafter can go without becoming a monster; she is not sure the Color Prince is lying about anything, which is the problem. Teia's secret starts to surface: she drafts paryl, an invisible colour beneath the spectrum the Chromeria admits to, useful for exactly the things nobody is supposed to do.

The jewelled dagger is finally identified. It is far older than the Chromeria, dating to the prophet who founded it, and it is a weapon built to take a drafter's magic away and store it. Kip has been carrying an artifact that several very dangerous people have spent lifetimes looking for, and Andross Guile is one of them. Kip also begins to learn what the Nine Kings cards really are: a few of them carry the memories of the people they depict, and a viewer can live them. Meanwhile a young red drafter named Zymun attaches himself to Liv and the rebellion, charming, ruthless and untethered. At the Chromeria, whispers about the Order of the Broken Eye, an old assassins' society the Chromeria insists it destroyed centuries ago, stop sounding like folklore.

Gavin sets about raising a fleet and an army with money and authority he does not really have, inventing his way around the shortfall as he goes. The Spectrum fights him at every step; Andross manoeuvres to marry his son to a useful house and to control whatever comes next. Karris and Gavin stop pretending about each other. Kip's squad becomes a unit rather than a collection of recruits, and Teia's paryl makes her quietly indispensable and quietly at risk. The Color Prince takes city after city in Atash, and the refugees start arriving faster than the satrapies can lie about it.

The recruits reach their final trials and Kip's squad is confirmed. Reports come back that the rebellion is not merely marching but building something at sea: a vast growing island of luxin the old texts call a bane, the sort of thing the histories say once housed gods. Gavin, whose remaining colours he now counts in single figures, decides the fleet must sail before it finishes forming. Zymun proves how dangerous he is to his own side as well as to the Chromeria's. Kip presses his grandfather across the card table for the one thing Andross will not trade, and starts to understand how much of his own history has been arranged.

Sun Day comes, the Chromeria's central festival, and with it the Freeing: the rite in which drafters who have reached the end of their span kneel before the Prism and are killed by him rather than be allowed to break and become wights. Felia Guile is one of them. She asks for it, and her son performs it, and before she dies she leaves him things about his family and its arrangements that he did not know and cannot now check. The ceremony is also the moment the Order of the Broken Eye chooses to show that it is real and inside the Chromeria's walls. Kip sees the Freeing for what it is, and so does everyone else who has been arguing that the Color Prince is simply wrong.

Gavin marries Karris, publicly and quickly, refusing the match his father had arranged and accepting the cost of that refusal. Then he sails. The bane has finished rising in the sea off Atash, a floating body of luxin large enough to be mistaken for land, and the rebellion is gathered around it: something is being grown inside it, and the old accounts agree on what happens if it is allowed to be born. Gavin's plan requires him to spend colours he no longer has. Kip goes with the fleet. Liv is on the other side of the water, close enough to the thing being made to understand exactly what her side is doing.

The battle is fought around Ru and out over the water. The rebellion's wights and cannon maul the Chromeria's fleet, and the fighting on land goes badly enough that the city cannot be held either. Gavin reaches the bane. Destroying it means putting more into one working than any drafter is built to survive, and he does it anyway, unmaking the island of luxin and the god forming inside it before it can draw breath. Kip is in the fighting and comes out of it alive. When the sea closes over the wreck of the bane, the Prism's magic is simply gone: he cannot draft a single colour, and there is no one left on the water who knows to look for him.

Gunner, a pirate cannoneer with an old grudge against the Prism and an unreliable grip on reality, pulls a half-drowned man out of the sea and keeps him. Gavin Guile, drained, unrecognised and without a scrap of magic, becomes cargo. The Seven Satrapies are told their Prism died at Ru. Karris is a Guile by marriage and a widow by every account she is given; Andross Guile is left with an empty office to fill and a grandson he has not decided what to do with; Kip comes home with the knife, a squad, and the beginning of an idea about what his family has actually done. Liv is too far inside the rebellion to walk back out of it. Beneath the Chromeria the real Gavin Guile breaks another cell wall, and another colour is taken from the brother who put him there.

characters.description: Driven off the Jaspers by his own grandfather, Kip arrives in the Blood Forest with a squad, a wife he barely knows, an ancient magic-stealing knife and no authority whatsoever. He is a polychrome with an unusual gift for reading people and for will-casting, and he is about to find out whether a boy who has never commanded anything can raise an army in a satrapy the rest of the world has written off.
characters.name: Kip

characters.description: The man the satrapies believe died at Ru, in truth Dazen Guile, who took his brother's name after the False Prism's War. He is blind, without a single colour, and shut in the deepest of the coloured cells beneath the Chromeria: the prison he designed himself, for the brother he replaced. Nobody outside that room knows he is alive.
characters.name: Gavin Guile

characters.description: The White: head of the Chromeria's administration, decades younger than anyone who has held the office before her, mourning a husband she was married to for a matter of weeks and presiding over a war she is losing. She was raised to the post by her dying predecessor precisely because she is not one of the Spectrum's own, and every Color on that council knows it.
characters.name: Karris Guile

characters.description: Head of House Guile, the Spectrum's Red, and now the most powerful man in the Seven Satrapies by some distance. With the war going badly he is pressing for promachos, the emergency office that suspends normal government and puts one man in charge of everything, and there is nobody left with the standing to stop him.
characters.name: Andross Guile

characters.description: A Blackguard and paryl drafter living as a member of the Order of the Broken Eye, the assassins' society she was sent to infiltrate. Her handler is the White, her cover requires her to do the Order's work, and the deeper she goes the fewer people there are who could confirm which side she is actually on. She hunts for the Order's hidden head, known only as the Old Man of the Desert.
characters.name: Teia

characters.description: Kip's wife by a marriage arranged in a hurry for the alliances it bought. A Malargos of Ruthgar, trained from childhood in negotiation and court politics, she is the reason anyone in the Blood Forest will listen to Kip at all, and she is far more use to him as a diplomat than he initially understands. The marriage itself is unfinished business between them.
characters.name: Tisis Malargos

characters.description: Kip's squad commander and conscience, a Blackguard by training and instinct who left the Jaspers rather than leave Kip. He wants the group to be something honourable, and he holds it to that standard whether or not the war allows it.
characters.name: Cruxer

characters.description: The squad's engineer, a multi-coloured drafter who would rather solve a problem with a mechanism than a sword, and who keeps producing devices that turn out to matter more than anyone expected.
characters.name: Ben-hadad

characters.description: The squad's archer: laconic, unsentimental about killing, and the best shot any of them have seen. He is not much interested in the moral arguments the others keep having.
characters.name: Winsen

characters.description: The leader of the rebellion that now holds Tyrea, Atash and much of the Blood Forest, a burned man seamed with every colour of luxin who no longer bothers with the title of prince. He preaches the end of the Chromeria and the Freeing, and he is deliberately growing the banes, the floating islands of luxin in which the old gods can be seeded.
characters.name: The White King

characters.description: The Prism-elect: charming in public, a murderer in private, and the son Karris bore and lost before the war. He is what the Chromeria has instead of a Prism, and he intends to be more than a figurehead.
characters.name: Zymun

characters.description: Aliviana Danavis, once a Chromeria student, now something the Chromeria has no vocabulary for. She works at the banes, where the rebellion is growing the vessels the old gods were said to inhabit, and she has stopped thinking of herself as anyone's subordinate.
characters.name: Aliviana Danavis

characters.description: The former commander of the Blackguard, a Parian of immense reputation who has lost both the Prism he was sworn to and his faith in the institution that employed him. His own country has a claim on him that he has spent his whole career refusing.
characters.name: Ironfist

characters.description: The Order of the Broken Eye's most accomplished assassin and Teia's teacher, a paryl drafter who moves unseen, keeps his own rituals, and collects the teeth of the people he kills. He is fond of Teia, which is not a safe thing to be.
characters.name: Murder Sharp

recaps.ending: Karris learns what her marriage actually was: the man she married is Dazen Guile, who took his dead brother's name, face and office after the False Prism's War and has been lying to her, and to everyone, for sixteen years. Gavin himself comes to the end of his descent through the cells he built, blind and without magic, and is out of that prison alive by the close of the book, no longer Prism and no longer anyone the satrapies think exists. Andross Guile holds the Chromeria as promachos, with Zymun installed as Prism-elect and Karris as a White with the title but not the power. Teia is further inside the Order of the Broken Eye than anyone can retrieve her from, still hunting its hidden head. Kip finishes the book as a war leader with a real army, a liberated city and a name in the Blood Forest, and with a marriage to Tisis that has become an actual partnership. On the other side, the White King's forces are still growing their banes, and Aliviana Danavis has taken a seed crystal and become something that is not a drafter any more, an old god of superviolet reborn under the name Ferrilux. The last defensible ground in the north is Kip's, the Jaspers are Andross's, and the gods are coming back.
recaps.in_short: Blind, powerless and given up for dead, Gavin is imprisoned in the deepest of the cells he built beneath the Chromeria and works his way down through them, forced back through everything the war cost. Above him, Andross Guile has himself made promachos and rules the Seven Satrapies outright, with the murderous Zymun as Prism-elect and Karris holding the White's title without its authority. Teia lives as an assassin of the Order of the Broken Eye, killing to hold a cover nobody can confirm, hunting the Order's hidden master. Kip and Tisis, exiled to the Blood Forest, raise an irregular army out of foresters, ghosts and refugees, break the siege of the city of Dunbheo, and turn a marriage of convenience into a real one. The White King's armies keep taking ground and his banes keep growing, and Aliviana Danavis takes a seed crystal and ascends as Ferrilux, an old god returned. By the end Karris has learned that her husband is Dazen, not Gavin, and Gavin is out of the cells alive with nothing left of what he was.

recaps.text: Previously: the Prism who was lost at Ru was really Dazen Guile, who beat his brother in the False Prism's War, took Gavin's name and office, and kept the real Gavin alive in nested coloured cells beneath the Chromeria. Stripped of every colour destroying the rebellion's bane, he was enslaved, escaped, and made it home only for his father Andross to blind him and lock him in that same prison. No one knows he is alive. Orea Pullawr died and Karris, widowed within weeks of marrying, was raised to the White. Andross produced Zymun as Prism-elect: a charming murderer who is also the son Karris bore and lost before the war. Teia, a Blackguard and the only known paryl drafter, was sent into the Order of the Broken Eye, the assassins' society the Chromeria pretended it had destroyed, and is still inside it with a stolen invisibility cloak and no way to prove her loyalty. Kip, hunted off the Jaspers by his grandfather, fled with his squad and married Tisis Malargos for the alliances it bought. The Color Prince, now calling himself the White King, holds Tyrea and Atash and is growing banes, the floating islands of luxin in which the old gods were said to be seeded. Liv Danavis works for him. Kip still carries the ancient knife that takes a drafter's magic.

Gavin wakes blind in a cell of his own design, fed through a slot, with no magic, no light and no way to tell how long he has been there. The only route he has is down: the cells are stacked, and each one has to be broken through. Above him, the Chromeria is being reorganised around a war it is losing. Karris takes up the White's office and discovers immediately that the Spectrum regards her as an inconvenient appointment rather than a superior. Kip, Tisis and the squad arrive in the Blood Forest, a satrapy already half overrun, and find no army, no chain of command and no obvious reason for anyone there to take orders from a disgraced Guile bastard.

Andross Guile presses the Spectrum to make him promachos, the wartime office that suspends the ordinary government of the satrapies and hands one man everything, and the war gives him all the argument he needs. Karris fights it and loses. Zymun, as Prism-elect, begins testing how far his position lets him go, and it becomes clear he is a danger to his own side and to his mother personally. In the Blood Forest, Kip starts gathering what is left: forest irregulars, refugees, hunters, a few drafters, people with nothing to go back to. Teia takes the Order's work as it is given to her, because refusing a job is how a spy is identified.

The rebellion's leader is Koios White Oak, Karris's own brother, believed burned to death in the fire that destroyed her family's estate before the war and blamed on Dazen Guile. He survived, and the White King's campaign is as much a family reckoning as a revolution. Karris has to run a war against her brother while the office above her is held by her father-in-law. Kip's ragged force starts to look like an army and starts winning small engagements, and Kip discovers he can will-cast, imposing his will through luxin in a way the Chromeria does not teach. His marriage to Tisis is still, awkwardly, a marriage on paper only.

Gavin breaks down into the next cell and the next, and blindness plus isolation stop being separable from memory: the descent forces him back through the war, what he did to win it, and what he did afterwards to keep the name he took. Teia is ordered to kill for the Order in ways she cannot square with anything, and her hunt narrows toward the Old Man of the Desert, the hidden head nobody in the Order has seen. Kip's army moves on Dunbheo, a Blood Forest city under siege by the White King's forces and being sold out from inside by its own council. Andross, now with the power he wanted, begins spending it.

Kip takes Dunbheo. The siege is broken by a combination of irregular warfare, Tisis's negotiating and Kip's willingness to do things no Chromeria-trained drafter would, and the city ends up his, which makes him a lord in fact whether or not anyone confirms it. The Blood Forest starts calling his force by a name. Karris, boxed in politically, turns to the one thing the White really controls, information, and starts pulling on the threads her predecessor left her, including the question of what exactly happened at the end of the False Prism's War. Zymun makes his first serious attempt to remove her.

The White King's armies press on the Blood Forest and his banes keep growing out at sea, each one a vessel for something the old accounts call a god. Liv is at the heart of that work and is offered the last step. Teia, deep enough in the Order to be trusted with its secrets, learns how far its reach goes and how long it has been inside the Chromeria's institutions rather than merely opposed to them. Kip and Tisis stop being allies and become a marriage. Gavin, still descending, runs out of versions of the war he can tell himself and has to account for what he actually did to his brother.

Aliviana Danavis takes a seed crystal at a bane and stops being a drafter at all: she comes out of it as Ferrilux, one of the old gods of superviolet returned to the world in a human body. The White King now has powers on his side that the Chromeria's doctrine says cannot exist. Kip consolidates the Blood Forest and prepares for a war on a scale his irregulars were never built for. Karris closes on the truth she has been circling. Teia is left holding what she has learned with nobody to hand it to, and the Order's plans for the Chromeria enter a new phase.

Karris finds out what her marriage really was. Her husband is Dazen Guile: he killed or replaced his brother at the end of the war, took Gavin's name, face and office, and lied to her and to the whole of the Seven Satrapies for sixteen years. Gavin comes to the bottom of the prison he built and is out of it alive by the close of the book, blind, without a colour to his name, and no longer the man any of the titles refer to. Andross Guile holds the satrapies as promachos with Zymun as his Prism-elect, and Karris keeps the White's title and very little of its power. Teia is beyond recall inside the Order, still hunting its master. Kip ends the book with an army, a liberated city, a name in the Blood Forest and a wife who is now a partner. Facing all of it: a White King who is Karris's own brother, banes still ripening at sea, and a returned god in Ferrilux.

characters.description: A son of the sky god and former Roman praetor, disciplined and dutiful, with power over wind and lightning. Now firmly one of the seven, he leads by example and has made peace with belonging to both the Greek and Roman worlds. As the crew closes on the final confrontation with Gaea, he braces the group for the sacrifices the prophecy seems to demand.
characters.name: Jason Grace

characters.description: A daughter of Aphrodite whose charmspeak can command with a word, now confident and battle-tested. Loyal to Jason and her friends, she trusts her own courage and cunning as much as her power, and she carries a growing dread about how the fight against the earth goddess will end.
characters.name: Piper McLean

characters.description: A son of Hephaestus, fire-wielder and builder of the warship Argo II, still masking loneliness with jokes. Sworn to return one day for the immortal Calypso, he throws himself into inventing a way to defeat Gaea, quietly hatching a risky plan he keeps from the others.
characters.name: Leo Valdez

characters.description: A son of the sea god and one of the most seasoned of the seven, hardened by his passage through Tartarus with Annabeth. Powerful over water and fiercely loyal, he stands ready for the last battle, shadowed by the darkness he saw in the pit.
characters.name: Percy Jackson

characters.description: A daughter of Athena and the crew's keenest strategist, tempered by surviving Tartarus at Percy's side. Clear-headed and resolute, she plans the demigods' moves against Gaea and the giants as the quest drives toward its climax.
characters.name: Annabeth Chase

characters.description: A daughter of Pluto who commands metals, gems, and the mist, her magic much surer than when the quest began. Gentle but courageous, she uses illusion and underworld insight to protect the crew as they approach the seat of the earth goddess's power.
characters.name: Hazel Levesque

characters.description: A son of Mars, shapeshifter and archer, grown into a capable leader far from the anxious boy he once was, though his life is still tied to a fragile length of wood. Steadfast and brave, devoted to Hazel, he takes on the burdens of command as the Romans and the final battle loom.
characters.name: Frank Zhang

characters.description: A son of the underworld god who commands the dead and shadow-travels, one of the trio racing to carry the Athena Parthenos statue home to prevent a war between the camps. Solitary and drained by using his powers, he pushes himself past his limits, carrying private grief and a secret he guards closely.
characters.name: Nico di Angelo

characters.description: A praetor of the Roman camp and daughter of a war goddess, disciplined and honorable, who has taken on the perilous mission of bringing the Athena Parthenos to Camp Half-Blood as a peace offering. Burdened by leadership and by a lonely sense of duty, she pushes herself relentlessly to hold the fragile hope of Greek and Roman unity together.
characters.name: Reyna

characters.description: The primordial earth goddess, on the verge of waking fully. Speaking through the land and through dreams, she marshals her giants for a final assault and seeks the blood of demigods to complete her rising and reclaim the world from the gods. She is the ultimate enemy the seven must stop before she draws her first waking breath.
characters.name: Gaea

recaps.ending: The two efforts succeed together. Reyna, Nico, and Coach Hedge deliver the Athena Parthenos to Camp Half-Blood just as the Roman legion is about to attack, and the statue's arrival reconciles the Greek and Roman demigods, ending the threat of war between them. In Athens, Gaea awakens and the giants rise, but the reunited camps and the gods, whose warring Greek and Roman natures are finally settled, join the seven in battle. Jason and Piper seize Gaea and lift her into the sky, severing her from the earth that is the source of her strength, and Leo strikes the helpless goddess with a blast of fire, unmaking her and ending the war. Leo, who had secretly obtained a physician's cure, appears to die in the blast, but the cure revives him, and he flies away on the restored bronze dragon Festus to rescue the immortal Calypso from her hidden island as he had sworn. The prophecy of the seven is fulfilled: Gaea is defeated, the giants are scattered, and the Greek and Roman camps stand united in peace. Percy and Annabeth, having survived Tartarus, look toward an ordinary future together. Nico, having let go of a long-held secret grief, chooses to stay at Camp Half-Blood and make a place among friends. In a closing surprise, Leo returns alive, Calypso at his side, reuniting with the crew who had mourned him.
recaps.in_short: In the final book, the seven demigods race to reach Athens and stop Gaea from waking, while Reyna, Nico, and Coach Hedge carry the Athena Parthenos statue across the world to reconcile the Greek and Roman camps before they go to war. Both journeys are hounded by giants and by the ancient hunter Orion. Leo secretly builds a device meant to defeat Gaea and quietly prepares to sacrifice himself, having obtained a means that might, or might not, bring him back. In Athens the giants gather and Gaea begins to rise from the earth. The gods, whose split Greek and Roman personalities have paralyzed them, are freed to help once the two camps are reconciled. In the climactic battle Jason and Piper lift Gaea off the ground into the air, cutting her off from the earth that gives her power, and Leo blasts her with fire, undoing her. Leo appears to die in the explosion but is revived by a physician's cure and flies off on the bronze dragon Festus to keep his promise to Calypso. Gaea is defeated, the camps are at peace, and the surviving heroes return home, with Leo turning up alive at the very end.

recaps.text: Previously: Seven demigods, Greek and Roman, were prophesied to stop the primordial earth goddess Gaea from waking and overthrowing the gods with her giants. To unite the two long-hostile camps, the goddess Hera swapped the heroes Jason and Percy and wiped their memories. Aboard the flying warship Argo II, the crew, Percy, Annabeth, Jason, Piper, Leo, Hazel, and Frank, sailed for the ancient lands to close the Doors of Death, which let Gaea's slain monsters return. Percy and Annabeth survived a passage through Tartarus, the abyss beneath the underworld, and the crew closed the Doors from both sides. To keep the Greek and Roman camps from destroying each other, Nico, the Roman leader Reyna, and the satyr Coach Hedge set out to carry a great statue, the Athena Parthenos, back to Camp Half-Blood as a token of peace. As this final book opens, the crew nears Athens for a last stand against Gaea, while the statue's bearers race to prevent a war between the camps.

characters.description: Mistress of Ingleside at Glen St. Mary, and by this stage of the series a woman whose name carries weight in the district. She appears chiefly in the short domestic scenes that link the stories, sitting with her family and reading her poems aloud, and in the stories themselves she is mostly offstage: a figure the neighbours quote, admire, envy, or resent according to their own natures. Several of the verses in the book are presented as her work.
characters.name: Anne Blythe

characters.description: The long-established doctor at Glen St. Mary, whose opinion the neighbourhood repeats as settled fact. He appears in the linking family scenes, dry and affectionate, and is talked about throughout the stories by people who have their own reasons for approving or disliking him.
characters.name: Gilbert Blythe

characters.description: The Ingleside housekeeper of a lifetime, elderly and unchanged in her loyalties, who takes part in the family conversations with her usual certainty about the failings of the neighbours and the merits of the Blythes.
characters.name: Susan Baker

characters.description: The poet of the Blythe family, present in the linking scenes of the first part and represented throughout the book by verses attributed to him. His poems are read aloud at Ingleside and are the occasion for much of the family's talk.
characters.name: Walter Blythe

characters.description: The eldest Blythe son, grown and settled, who appears in the family scenes and is referred to in the district as one of the Ingleside children the Glen has watched grow up.
characters.name: Jem Blythe

characters.description: The youngest Blythe daughter, grown up now, who takes part in the family conversations at Ingleside between the stories.
characters.name: Rilla Blythe

characters.description: The Blythe twins, grown women by the time of these stories, who appear in the linking scenes at Ingleside and are counted among the Glen's own.
characters.name: Nan and Di Blythe

recaps.ending: The book has no single plot to resolve. It closes at the end of its second part, after the war, with the Blythes older, the family circle reduced by Walter's death, and the last of the linking scenes at Ingleside given over to reading his verses and to the family's talk around them. The stories of the second part end as they began, in the private affairs of Glen St. Mary and Four Winds neighbours, several of them on a note of irony or plain bitterness rather than the reconciliations the earlier books preferred. The Blythes themselves are left as the district sees them: prosperous, respected, endlessly quoted, and privately carrying a loss the Glen mentions but does not feel. Taken as a whole the collection is Montgomery's closing word on the world of Avonlea and the Glen, published complete only long after her death, and it leaves that world intact but noticeably darker than she had drawn it before.
recaps.in_short: The last Anne book is not a novel but a collection: two parts of short stories set in and around Glen St. Mary and Four Winds, interleaved with poems attributed to Anne and Walter Blythe and with brief scenes of the Blythe family at Ingleside talking over those poems and their neighbours. The first part is set before the First World War and the second after it. The Blythes themselves stay mostly at the edges; the stories belong to the people of the district, who quote the doctor and his wife, measure themselves against Ingleside, and conduct their own courtships, feuds, deceptions, and reconciliations. The tone is markedly harder than in the earlier books, with more irony and more unhappiness allowed to stand. Walter's death in the war is the shadow across the second part, and his verses are read aloud in the family scenes. Montgomery sent the manuscript to her publisher at the very end of her life; a shortened version appeared decades later, and the complete text only in 2009.

recaps.text: Previously: Anne Shirley, brought up as an orphan at Green Gables in Avonlea, married Doctor Gilbert Blythe and raised their family at Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, with the housekeeper Susan Baker in charge of the kitchen. Their children are Jem, Walter, the twins Nan and Di, Shirley, and the youngest, Rilla, and the family's closest friends have long been the Meredith children of the Glen manse. The First World War took the young men of the district: Jem was taken prisoner and came home, and Walter, the poet of the family, was killed in France, leaving verses that were published and widely read.
